Almighty Father from Whom all goodness flows, grant unto us qualities of wisdom justice and tolerance, that we the civic leaders of this community may govern in harmony and concord.

This we ask in Thy name. 

We also remember and give thanks for those, our sons and daughters, who gave their lives for Australia. 

Lest we forget. 

Niina Marni is Kaurna for ' Welcome'. The City of Charles Sturt acknowledges and pays respect to the traditional custodians of the land, the Kaurna people of the Adelaide plains. We pay our respect to Elders past, present and emerging. We respect their spiritual beliefs and connections to land which are of continuing importance to the Kaurna people of today. We acknowledge the contributions and important role that Aboriginal people continue to play within our local community in Charles Sturt. We also respect the culture of Aboriginal people visiting from other areas of South Australia and Australia.

To inform Council of the release of the Draft Community Engagement Charter (May 2025) by the Office of Local Government for consultation, and to seek Council’s retrospective endorsement of a draft submission outlining the City of Charles Sturt’s response. 

Given the short consultation timeframe, Council Administration submitted the draft response on 24 June 2025 to ensure the feedback was considered within the required period.
 


Moved: Councillor Tom Scheffler
Seconded: Councillor Peter Ppiros

Motion


  1. That Council retrospectively endorse the submission (Appendix 2) provided to the Office of Local Government on 27 June 2025 in response to the Draft Community Engagement Charter (Appendix 1).

  2. That Council notes the submission was provided by Administration prior to the consultation deadline of 29 June 2025 due to timing constraints.

  3. That Council notes the intention of the Charter to inform future legislative requirements and engagement practices under the Local Government Act 1999.

Carried

Mayor Angela Evans has proposed an item of business to be submitted on behalf of Council for inclusion in the 2025 Local Government Association (LGA) Annual General Meeting (AGM) agenda. The 2025 LGA AGM is being held on Friday, 21 November 2025.



Moved: Councillor Senthil ChidambaranathanSeconded: Councillor Tom Scheffler

Motion

1. That Council supports the submission of the following proposed motion:

a. That the Annual General Meeting requests the LGA to advocate to the Minister for Transport to consider the inclusion of legislation to enable the Council to enforce long term parking controls of vehicles on Council roads.

b. That the Annual General Meeting requests the LGA to advocate to the Minister for Transport to consider the inclusion of legislation to enable the Council to enforce long term parking controls of vehicles on State roads.

Carried Unanimously

The Local Government Association of South Australia (LGA) has provided a quarterly delegations update which includes amendments that have been made due to legislative changes and require Councils' to update their delegations register.



Moved: Councillor Michael McEwen
Seconded: Councillor Stuart Ghent

Motion

  1. In exercise of the power contained in Section 44 of the Local Government Act 1999, the powers and functions under the Planning, Development and Infrastructure Act 2016 and statutory instruments made thereunder and specified in Appendix 1 to the report dated 14 July 2025 and titled 'Quarterly Update to Council's Delegations' (delegated to the person occupying the position of Chief Executive Officer of the Council) are hereby delegated this 14 day of July 2025, as set out in Appendix 1 subject to the conditions and/or limitations (if any) specified herein or in Appendix 1.
 
 The additional delegations will come into operation on 18 July 2025.
 
  1. In exercise of the power contained in Section 44 of the Local Government Act 1999, the powers and functions under the Planning, Development and Infrastructure Act 2016 and statutory instruments made thereunder and specified in Appendix 1 to the report dated 14 July 2025 and titled 'Quarterly Update to Council's Delegations' (delegated to the person occupying the position of Chief Executive Officer of the Council) are hereby amended this 14 day of July 2025, as set out in Appendix 1 subject to the conditions and/or limitations (if any) specified herein or in Appendix 1.
 
 The amendment of these delegations will come into operation on 18 July 2025.
  
  1. In exercise of the power contained in Section 44 of the Local Government Act 1999, the powers and functions under the Local Government (General) Regulations 2013 and Planning, Development and Infrastructure Act 2016 and specified in Appendix 1 are hereby revoked this 14 day of July 2025.
 
       The revocation of these delegations will be effective from 18 July 2025.
 
Carried Unanimously

Council, as a co-owner with the City of Port Adelaide Enfield of the regional subsidiary CAWRA, is now provided with CAWRA's draft budget for 2025/26 for comment as required under the Local Government Act 1999.

In accordance with the Local Government Act 1999 the CEO is recommending that this report be heard in confidence under Section 90(3)(b)(i) and (ii) and 90(3)(d)(i) and (ii) as information the disclosure of which could reasonably be expected to confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting, or proposing to conduct, business, or to prejudice the commercial position of the council; and would, on balance, be contrary to the public interest. Also, commercial information of a confidential nature (not being a trade secret) the disclosure of which could reasonably be expected to prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied the information, or to confer a commercial advantage on a third party; and would, on balance, be contrary to the public interest.


Moved: Councillor Edgar Agius
Seconded: Councillor George Turelli

Recommendation - Exclusion of the Public (from 8.07 PM)
That:
  1. Pursuant to Section 90(2) of the Local Government Act 1999, Council hereby orders that the public be excluded from attendance at this meeting, with the exception of the Chief Executive Officer, General Manager Engaged Community, General Manager City Futures, Acting General Manager City Operations, Acting General Manager Corporate Services, Manager Governance and Risk, Manager Community Engagement and Experience, Acting Manager Financial Services, Team Leader Governance and Risk, Governance Officer, and Senior Business Analyst currently in attendance at the meeting, in order to consider ITEM 11.1 CAWRA DRAFT ANNUAL BUDGET 2025/26 in confidence.

  2. In accordance with Section 90(3) of the Local Government Act 1999, Council is satisfied that it is necessary that the public be excluded to consider the information contained in the report ITEM 11.1 CAWRA DRAFT ANNUAL BUDGET 2025/26 on the following grounds:
b.
information the disclosure of which (i) could reasonably be expected to confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting, or proposing to conduct, business, or to prejudice the commercial position of the council; and (ii) would, on balance, be contrary to the public interest.

Recommended Action
  1. Accordingly, on this basis, the principle that meetings of the Council should be conducted in a place open to the public has been outweighed by the need to keep the information or discussion confidential.

Carried Unanimously

A request for an internal review of a Council decision made under Section 270 of the Local Government Act 1999 was received from a community member. The request was to review the decision of Council relating to the renaming of Croydon Avenue Reserve to Eileen Harris Reserve which was made by Council on 22 April 2024 (refer AMS 15/04/24, Item 4.19 and CL 22/04/24).


Moved: Councillor Alice Campbell
Seconded: Councillor Nicholas Le Lacheur

Motion

  1. That Council accepts the Section 270 Review report as prepared by the Team Leader Governance and Risk (Appendix 1).

  2. That Council having re-considered all the information before it at the time it made the decision, the information submitted by the applicant, and this report, and determines that the decision was the best and preferable decision.

  3. That Council has made the decision to take no further action in relation to this report.

  4. That the Chief Executive Officer writes to the complainant to advise of Council's decision.

Carried Unanimously

This report provides an overview of an unsolicited proposal (Appendix 1) submitted by Hydro2050 for the remediation of Torrens Lake using nanobubble technology and the response to the proposal.

Councillor Kelly Thomas left the meeting at 8:23 PM.
Councillor Kelly Thomas entered the meeting at 8:23 PM.

Moved: Councillor Kenzie van den NieuwelaarSeconded: Councillor Nicole Mazeika

Motion

  1. That Council notes the unsolicited proposal submitted by Hydro2050 Pty Ltd for nanobubble remediation of Torrens Lake (Appendix 1).

  2. That Council notes the feedback from Torrens Lake Cyanobacterial Advisory Committee (TLCAC) members, including the decisions of Green Adelaide, EPA, SA Water and Adelaide City Council who have all declined to further investigate and/or trial the Hydro2050 proposal further. 

  3. That Council notes growing community dissatisfaction and concern regarding the downstream and coastal environmental impacts of the current reactive management strategy of flushing the Torrens Lake to remove blue-green algae blooms.

  4. That Council writes to the Minister for Climate, Environment and Water, requesting consideration of funding for investigation and testing of innovative and proactive water quality technologies to address blue-green algae at its source to eliminate the need to flush contaminated water downstream into the marine environment and onto Adelaide’s beaches.

  5. That Council staff continue to advocate through the TLCAC for proactive upstream and lake interventions that prevent, rather than relocate (flush) water quality issues downstream impacting the lower reaches of the River Torrens and the marine environment at West Beach.

Carried Unanimously

Brief
The Strategic and Engagement Committee was held on Monday, 21 July 2025.

Moved: Councillor Nicole MazeikaSeconded: Councillor Nicholas Le Lacheur

That having considered the recommendations of the Committee which has read and considered the reports in the agenda related to all items, with the exception of Items 4.2 and 4.5:


4.1 SUBMISSION TO STATE GOVERNMENT PUBLIC TRANSPORT STRATEGY

Motion
 
That the Committee recommends to the Council:

  1.  That Council note the submission contained in Appendix 1 in response to the State Government’s Public Transport Strategy consultation, which has been provided to the Department for Infrastructure and Transport during the consultation period.

  2. That any response to Council's submission from State Government be brought to the Strategy and Engagement Committee for information and consideration as to next steps.
 

4.3 DRAFT DESIGN STANDARD 1 - ENGINEERING REQUIREMENTS FOR LAND DIVISIONS
 
Motion

  1. That the Committee recommends to Council that Council endorse the submission contained in Appendix 1 in relation to the draft Design Standard 1 - Engineering Requirements for Land Division.
 
4.4 WEST TORRENS CATCHMENT STORMWATER MANAGEMENT PLAN – ENDORSEMENT

Motion
 
To ensure the long-term responsible management of stormwater within the City of Charles Sturt in relation to the adjoining West Torrens catchment, that the Committee recommends to Council:
 
  1. That the West Torrens Stormwater Management Plan as presented in Appendix 1 be endorsed.

  2. That Council notes that during the next scheduled review, the City of Charles Sturt’s Water Infrastructure Asset Management Plan will be updated to incorporate the West Torrens Stormwater Management Plan.

  3. That Council notes that the West Torrens Stormwater Management Plan identifies stormwater works within the City of Charles Sturt, albeit projected to occur after a minimum of 10–15 years. Accordingly, there is no immediate requirement to adjust the Long-Term Financial Plan or allocate funding at this stage.

  4. That the City of West Torrens and other participating Councils be formally notified of this decision.
 
4.6 CONSIDER A DEVELOPMENT AT VARIANCE TO AN LMA - 2 BUCKNALL COURT TENNYSON AND ASSOCIATED PETITION

Motion
 
That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That Administration is currently seeking advice in relation to the mechanics of the Land Management Agreement.

  2. That a report will be brought to a future meeting of the Strategic and Engagement Committee at the appropriate time.

  3. That Administration will continue to communicate with the head petitioner in relation to decision timelines as the matter progresses. 

 

 
4.7 COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT FUNDED PROGRAMS
 
Motion

  1. That the report be received and noted.

 

Council adopts the recommendations of the Committee as printed in the Minutes of this Committee.


Carried Unanimously


Councillor Rachele Tullio entered the meeting at 7:04 PM.


Moved: Councillor Katriona KinsellaSeconded: Councillor Nicholas Le Lacheur

4.5 STRENGTHENING COMMUNITY IDENTITY THROUGH PLACE NAMING

This report constitutes a follow-up report to the decision of Council on 28/7/25 under Item 6.3 to defer a decision in relation to assignment of road names required by virtue of the division of land in Brompton.

Moved: Councillor Katriona KinsellaSeconded: Councillor Nicole Mazeika

Motion

  1. That Council acknowledges the historical significance of the former Brompton Gasworks site and its legacy in South Australia’s industrial development. Council also recognises the cultural importance of this land to the Kaurna people and notes that the site's developer MAB has indicated formal recognition of Kaurna heritage, including Kaurna naming of places and reserves, will occur through future engagement processes and integration into the landscape, public realm, and public art associated with the former Brompton Gasworks site.

 

  1. That Council endorses the following names for new public roads for stage one of the development created via the land division 24012194 in accordance with the following list:
  • Retort House Way
  • Stokers Lane
  • Gasworks Boulevard 
  • Bluestone Avenue / Lane (a 'spare' name if required following consultation with other external agencies).

 

  1. That Council notes that the assignment of road names for future stages of the division will be addressed in a subsequent report to Council, with further engagement in a workshop with Council Members on the Council led Place Naming project to occur prior to consideration of any new names.

Carried Unanimously

Council’s Animal Management Plan (the Plan) is a legally mandated strategic document required under the Dog and Cat Management Act 1995 (the Act). The current Plan, which guides Council’s approach to the management of dogs and cats in alignment with local community demographics, has been in effect for the period 2021–2025 and is due to expire at the end of this year.

In accordance with the Act, each Council must ensure that an Animal Management Plan is in place and maintained. This report outlines the final outcomes of Council’s current Animal Management Plan 2021–2025 and sets out the proposed community engagement approach to inform the development of the next Animal Management Plan for the period 2026–2030.

Moved: Councillor Kelly ThomasSeconded: Councillor Kenzie van den Nieuwelaar

Motion

  1. That Council acknowledges the finalisation and completion of the existing Animal Management Plan 2021-2025 as detailed in Appendix 1.
 
  1. That Council endorses the community consultation approach as detailed in Appendix 3, to seek feedback from the community for the proposed Animal Management Plan 2026-2030 as detailed in Appendix 2.
Carried Unanimously

Almighty Father from Whom all goodness flows, grant unto us qualities of wisdom justice and tolerance, that we the civic leaders of this community may govern in harmony and concord.

We also remember and give thanks for those, our sons and daughters, who gave their lives for Australia. 

Lest we forget. 

Niina Marni is Kaurna for ' Welcome'. The City of Charles Sturt acknowledges and pays respect to the traditional custodians of the land, the Kaurna people of the Adelaide plains. We pay our respect to Elders past, present and emerging. We respect their spiritual beliefs and connections to land which are of continuing importance to the Kaurna people of today. We acknowledge the contributions and important role that Aboriginal people continue to play within our local community in Charles Sturt. We also respect the culture of Aboriginal people visiting from other areas of South Australia and Australia.

 The Corporate Services Committee was held on Monday, 4 August 2025.

Moved: Councillor Alice CampbellSeconded: Councillor Nicholas Le Lacheur

That having considered the recommendations of the Committee which has read and considered the reports in the agenda related to items:

 

4.1 STRATEGIC PROCUREMENT UPDATE - PRESENTATION


Motion
 
  1. That the presentation be received and noted.

 4.2 UPDATE TO FEES AND CHARGES REGISTER
 
 Motion
 
 That the Committee recommends to the Council:
  
  1. That the amendments to the Fees and Charges Register 2025/26 be endorsed as identified in Appendix 1 and 2.

 4.3 ANNUAL REVIEW OF FINANCIAL POLICIES
 
 Motion
 
 That the Committee recommends to the Council:
  
  1. That the annual review of Council financial policies, such review not precluding any subsequent review, alteration or additional policy which Council may wish to make from time to time, including the next annual review scheduled for August 2026, be adopted.  

  2. That the specific policies as amended through track changes and detailed in Appendices 1 through 16 to the report be endorsed and adopted and incorporated into Council's Policy Register.

 


 4.4 POLICIES FOR REVIEW - MINOR CHANGES ONLY
 
 Motion
 
  1. That the Committee recommends to Council that the revised policies, listed below, be adopted;
  • Council Members' Training and Development Policy in Appendix 1
  • Flag Pole Usage Policy in Appendix 2
  • Telecommunications and Electricity Infrastructure on Council Land Policy in Appendix 3
  • Memorials Policy in Appendix 4
 

Council adopts the recommendations of the Committee as printed in the Minutes of this Committee.

Carried Unanimously

This report outlines a time sensitive opportunity for Council to consider and support funding proposals from Western Strikers Soccer Club (WSSC) and Henley & Grange Baseball Club (HGBC) which will enable both clubs to leverage funding through combined contributions from Council, the clubs, and Office for Recreation, Sport and Racing (ORSR) via the 'Power of Her' funding program. The clubs are seeking Council’s financial support towards lighting upgrades at Carnegie North & South Reserve (WSSC) and an indoor training facility at West Lakes Shore Oval (HGBC). 

Moved: Councillor Kelly ThomasSeconded: Councillor Stuart Ghent

Motion

  1. That Council includes a funding contribution of $150K within the draft 2026/27 annual budget towards the Henley & Grange Baseball Club's proposed $330K new indoor batting/training facility, subject to the Club securing matched grant funding.

  2. That Council includes a funding contribution of $145K within the draft 2026/27 annual budget towards the Western Strikers Soccer Club's proposed $700K sports lighting upgrade at Carnegie North & South Reserves, subject to the Club successfully securing matched grant funding.
Carried Unanimously

Metropolitan Coastal Councils are preparing to send a delegation of representatives to Canberra to call on the Federal Government to recognise the algal bloom event as a climate-accelerated environmental crisis and seek commitment to an urgent coordinated national response. Mayor Evans is requesting Council's support to represent the City of Charles Sturt in Canberra from Wednesday 27 August to Friday 29 August 2025.

Material Declaration of Interest

Mayor - Angela Evans declared a material conflict of interest pursuant to Section 75C of the Local Government Act for Item 6.4. The nature of Mayor - Angela Evans' material conflict is that the item recommends Council financially support the cost of her travel expenses to Canberra for meetings with Federal Ministers regarding the impacts of the Southern Barrier Reef algal bloom on coastal councils including those coastal areas located within the City of Charles Sturt and left the meeting.

Mayor - Angela Evans left the meeting at 7:48 PM

In the absence of Mayor - Angela Evans, the Deputy Mayor - Edgar Agius, took the Chair at 7:48 PM.


Moved: Councillor George TurelliSeconded: Councillor Alice Campbell

Motion

  1. That Council approves Mayor Evans' attendance in Canberra to represent the City of Charles Sturt's interests in advocating for Federal Government's commitment to a national response to the algal bloom event from Wednesday 27 August to Friday 29 August 2025, at an estimated cost of $1,500.

  1. That Council approves Mayor Evans to be a party signatory to the Draft Proposal for Federal Government Action on the South Australian Algal Bloom Crisis (Appendix 1) to be submitted to the Federal Government prior to the delegation to Canberra, acknowledging that the Draft Proposal may include changes prior to being finalised.

  2. That any further iterations to the Draft Proposal will be included within the Minutes.

  3. That Mayor Evans table a written report to Council within a 30-day period from the date of return, outlining the key outcomes from Ministerial discussions.

Carried Unanimously

At 7:52 PM  Mayor Evans entered the meeting and resumed her seat and the Chair.

Almighty Father from Whom all goodness flows, grant unto us qualities of wisdom justice and tolerance, that we the civic leaders of this community may govern in harmony and concord.

This we ask in Thy name. 

We also remember and give thanks for those, our sons and daughters, who gave their lives for Australia. 

Lest we forget. 

Niina Marni is Kaurna for ' Welcome'. The City of Charles Sturt acknowledges and pays respect to the traditional custodians of the land, the Kaurna people of the Adelaide plains. We pay our respect to Elders past, present and emerging. We respect their spiritual beliefs and connections to land which are of continuing importance to the Kaurna people of today. We acknowledge the contributions and important role that Aboriginal people continue to play within our local community in Charles Sturt. We also respect the culture of Aboriginal people visiting from other areas of South Australia and Australia.

 The Operations Committee was held on Monday, 18 August 2025.
Moved: Councillor Senthil ChidambaranathanSeconded: Councillor Edgar Agius

That having considered the recommendations of the Committee which has read and considered the reports in the agenda related to items:

 

4.1 CITY OPERATIONS CAPITAL WORKS & OPERATING PROGRAM VARIATIONS
 
Motion
 
That the Committee recommends to the Council: 
 
  1. That the following variation to the Capital Works Program be approved and budgets or scope adjusted accordingly:
    1. Budgeted expenditure for 2025/26 Council Building Renewals Project 3807 remain unchanged, with the project scope change to include replacement of the rusted bullnose veranda sheets at Bower Cottages.

    2. Budgeted expenditure for 2025/26 Council Building Renewals Project 3823 remain unchanged, with the project scope change to include the renewal works required on the Barry Jarman and Percy Fox grandstands located at Woodville Oval.

4.2 GLENEAGLES RESERVE STORMWATER DETENTION PROJECT STAGE 1 & RESERVE UPGRADE - QUARTERLY UPDATE REPORT
 
Motion
 
  1. That the Committee recommends to Council that a project completion report be presented to the Operations Committee once the project is completed in the first half of 2026.
 
4.3 TREE CANOPY IMPROVEMENT STRATEGY PROGRESS UPDATE 
 
Motion
 
That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That the progress of the implementation of actions contained within the Tree Canopy Improvement Strategy be noted and that implementation of on-ground tree planting works be noted.
 
  1. That further updates on the progress of the Strategy be presented to the Operations Committee annually at the end of each planting season for the financial year.
 
4.4 STREETSCAPE UPGRADE PROJECTS - QUARTERLY UPDATE REPORT
 
Motion
 
  1. That the Committee recommends to Council that continued updates on the Chief Street, Hawker Street and Renown Park Living Streets Streetscape Projects be presented to the Operations Committee.
 
4.5 ST CLAIR RECREATION CENTRE QUARTERLY REPORT - APRIL TO JUNE 2025 QUARTER  
 
Motion
 
That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That Council notes the YMCA's Performance Report for the April to June 2025 quarter. 
 
  1. That further quarterly reports be presented to the Operations Committee.

This report outlines the current challenges and opportunities associated with the Beverley Depot. It canvasses the redevelopment options that have been considered and recommends a preferred option that addresses the identified risks and provides an improved long-term outcome for both Council operations and the Beverley community compared with the original proposal.

In accordance with the Local Government Act 1999, it is recommended that the report be considered under Section 90(3)(b) and 90(3)(d) as the information, the disclosure of which could reasonably be expected to confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom council is conducting, or proposing to conduct, business, or to prejudice the commercial position of council; and is commercial information of a confidential nature (not being a trade secret), the disclosure of which could reasonably be expected to prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied the information, or confer a commercial advantage on a third party. The disclosure of this information would, on balance, be contrary to the public interest.

Moved: Councillor Stuart Ghent
Seconded: Councillor Nicholas Le Lacheur

That (from 7.47 PM):

  1. Pursuant to Section 90(2) of the Local Government Act 1999, Council hereby orders that the public be excluded from attendance at this meeting, with the exception of the Chief Executive Officer, General Manager Corporate Services, General Manager City Futures, General Manager Engaged Community, General Manager City Operations, Manager Governance and Risk, Manager Community Engagement and Experience, Manager City Utilities, Manager Construction and Delivery, Manager Community Connections, Manager People and Culture, Manager City Maintenance, Manager Community Health and Safety, and Team Leader Governance and Risk currently in attendance at the meeting, in order to consider ITEM 11.1 - BEVERLEY DEPOT REBUILD UPDATE in confidence.

  2. In accordance with Section 90(3) of the Local Government Act 1999, Council is satisfied that it is necessary that the public be excluded to consider the information contained in the report ITEM 11.1 - BEVERLEY DEPOT REBUILD UPDATE on the following grounds:
b.
information the disclosure of which (i) could reasonably be expected to confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting, or proposing to conduct, business, or to prejudice the commercial position of the council; and (ii) would, on balance, be contrary to the public interest.
d.
commercial information of a confidential nature (not being a trade secret) the disclosure of which (i) could reasonably be expected to prejudice the commercial position of the person who supplied the information, or to confer a commercial advantage on a third party; and (ii) would, on balance, be contrary to the public interest.

Recommended Action
  1. Accordingly, on this basis, the principle that meetings of the Council should be conducted in a place open to the public has been outweighed by the need to keep the information or discussion confidential.
Carried Unanimously


Moved: Councillor Michael McEwen
Seconded: Councillor Edgar Agius

Acknowledging that the existing Beverley Depot building has reached the end of its useful life, contains asbestos, and poses ongoing safety and maintenance risks; and further noting that alternative locations in the Beverley precinct are not viable due to contamination from prior non-Council land uses and poor ground conditions, and that all other cost-effective options have been explored, it is recommended that Council:
 
  1. Endorse the demolition of the existing Beverley Depot building and the procurement of new temporary office and workshop accommodation, within the existing approved budget, commencing in the 2025/26 financial year.
 
  1. Endorse that cash funding for Part 1 will be provided from the existing approved budget, comprising a portion of the Beverley Depot Redevelopment capital project funding (Project #3547 – $4.5M) and the Carpark Renewal project funding (Project #3581 – $450K), with the balance of these approved funds expected to be carried forward to 2026/27 as part of the budget for the broader redevelopment project.
 
  1. Provide in-principle support for the concept plans at Appendix 1, noting:
 
  • The potential for improvement of Toogood Reserve open space;
  • The opportunity to create additional green space on the Beverley Depot site (as per details in recommendation 6), complementing the potential acquisition of adjacent land from DIT on William Street; and
  • That these initiatives would improve green space distribution and community liveability in Beverley.

  1. Endorse the preparation of a budget bid for the concept plan to be included in the 2026/27 Annual Business Plan and Budget process, for consideration alongside other Council priorities and subject to community consultation.
 
  1. Require that a Prudential Review of the project, in accordance with Section 48 of the Local Government Act 1999 and Council’s Prudential Review Policy, be undertaken at the appropriate juncture. 
 

 

  1. Ensure that the Prudential Review includes possible mechanisms to offset future construction costs, including:
  
  • The potential sale of the existing depot site;
  • The likelihood and conditions of such a sale; and
  • Options to secure highest and best use outcomes, community benefit, and sound cost–benefit results.

  1. Request that staff provide a further report to Council in late 2025 / early 2026, presenting the prudential report and detailed design outcomes prior to finalising the 2026/27 budget submission.

  2. That staff investigate the opportunity to purchase the property on the corner of Toogood Avenue and William Street, Beverley.
 
  1. That ITEM 11.1 - BEVERLEY DEPOT REBUILD UPDATE having been considered in confidence pursuant to section 90(3)(b)(i) and (ii) and 90(3)(d)(i) and (ii) of the Local Government Act 1999, the Council hereby orders, in accordance with section 91(7) of the Local Government Act 1999 that Appendix 3 and 4 of this item be kept confidential until any subsequent land sale associated with the construction of a new Depot is completed.


Carried Unanimously

That Council, acknowledging the importance of immunisation as a critical public health measure, and recognising both the complexity of providing direct immunisation services and the need to maintain strong immunisation outcomes within our community to meet our obligations under the South Australian Public Health Act 2011:

Almighty Father from Whom all goodness flows, grant unto us qualities of wisdom justice and tolerance, that we the civic leaders of this community may govern in harmony and concord.

This we ask in Thy name. 

We also remember and give thanks for those, our sons and daughters, who gave their lives for Australia. 

Lest we forget. 

Niina Marni is Kaurna for ' Welcome'. The City of Charles Sturt acknowledges and pays respect to the traditional custodians of the land, the Kaurna people of the Adelaide plains. We pay our respect to Elders past, present and emerging. We respect their spiritual beliefs and connections to land which are of continuing importance to the Kaurna people of today. We acknowledge the contributions and important role that Aboriginal people continue to play within our local community in Charles Sturt. We also respect the culture of Aboriginal people visiting from other areas of South Australia and Australia.

Motion 
 
  1. That the presentation be received and noted.

  1. That the report be received and noted.
  2. That a work in progress carry forward budget of $25,609,696 as detailed in Appendix 1 to this report be approved and included in the 2025/26 budget to complete capital projects from 2024/25.

 


4.3 REVIEW OF AUTHORISED OFFICERS/PERSONS/SIGNATORIES


Motion 
 
That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That the review of Authorised Signatories and Authorised Persons/Officers, and such review not precluding any subsequent review, alteration or additional appointment which the Council, or the Chief Executive Officer (or its delegate), may make from time to time, including the next annual review, be adopted.
 
  1. That, without derogating in any way from actions taken by Authorised Signatories and/or Authorised Persons/Officers, and effective from Monday 8 September 2025 all appointments made prior pursuant to:
 
  • Section 58(2) of the Burial and Cremation Act 2013

  • Section 85(3) of the Environment Protection Act 1993
  • Section 6(3) of the Expiation of Offences Act 1996

  • Section 94(1) of the Food Act 2001

  • Section 12(3) of the Local Nuisance and Litter Control Act 2016
  • Section 210(1)(a) and 210(1)(b) of the Planning, Development and Infrastructure Act 2016
  • Section 35(1a) of the Road Traffic Act 1961
  • Section 44(1) of the South Australian Public Health Act 2011
  • Section 21(1) of the Supported Residential Facilities Act 1992
  • Section 41(1) of the Water Industry Act 2012
 
               have been reviewed.
  
  1. That pursuant to Section 44 of the Local Government Act 1999, and effective from Tuesday 9 September 2025, Council authorise the officers listed in Appendix 1 to sign the respective documentation on behalf of Council in accordance with any conditions/limitations detailed in Appendix 1.
  
  1. That Council appoint and authorise the persons listed in the Authorised Persons/Officers listing as detailed in Appendix 2, pursuant to the relevant legislation and with any conditions/limitations stipulated in Appendix 2. These appointments and authorisations are effective from Tuesday 9 September 2025.
 
  1. That all previous authorisations and appointments of Authorised Signatories and Authorised Persons/Officers are revoked as of Tuesday 9 September 2025.

4.4 POLICIES FOR REVIEW - MINOR CHANGES ONLY 

 

Motion
 
  1. That the Committee recommends to Council that the revised policies, listed below, be adopted;
  • Insurance Policy in Appendix 1
  • Path Policy in Appendix 2
  • Encroachment Policy in Appendix 3
  

Council adopts the recommendations of the Committee as printed in the Minutes of this Committee.

Carried Unanimously

To present the City of Charles Sturt’s Organisational Plan 2025 - 2030 for Council endorsement. This report also outlines the revised Quarterly Performance Reporting associated with the Organisational Plan and aligned to financial quarters, to provide transparent updates on progress toward the Community Vision outcomes.

Moved: Councillor Nicole Mazeika
Seconded: Councillor Nicholas Le Lacheur

Motion

  1. That Council endorses the City of Charles Sturt Organisational Plan 2025 - 2030 as provided in Appendix 1.
 
  1. That Council endorses the revised Quarterly Performance Reporting, aligned to Council’s financial quarterly cycle and focused on progress toward the Community Vision 2040 outcomes and Organisational Plan commitments.


    Councillor - Kelly Thomas entered the meeting at 7:07 PM

Carried Unanimously

In accordance with the Local Government Act 1999, the CEO is recommending that this report be heard in confidence under Section 90(3)(h) and (i) as the information contains legal advice, and information relating to actual litigation, or litigation that the council or council committee believes on reasonable grounds will take place, involving the council or an employee of the council.

h.
legal advice.
i.
information relating to actual litigation, or litigation that the council or council committee believes on reasonable grounds will take place, involving the council or an employee of the council.

Carried Unanimously

Carried Unanimously

Almighty Father from Whom all goodness flows, grant unto us qualities of wisdom justice and tolerance, that we the civic leaders of this community may govern in harmony and concord.

We also remember and give thanks for those, our sons and daughters, who gave their lives for Australia. 

Lest we forget. 

Niina Marni is Kaurna for ' Welcome'. The City of Charles Sturt acknowledges and pays respect to the traditional custodians of the land, the Kaurna people of the Adelaide plains. We pay our respect to Elders past, present and emerging. We respect their spiritual beliefs and connections to land which are of continuing importance to the Kaurna people of today. We acknowledge the contributions and important role that Aboriginal people continue to play within our local community in Charles Sturt. We also respect the culture of Aboriginal people visiting from other areas of South Australia and Australia.

To inform Council of recent anti-social behaviours by different groups occurring at the Ovingham Underpass/Karrarendi Yerta Kadla, the holistic response currently being implemented and coordinated by City of Charles Sturt and shared with the City of Prospect, SAPOL and other government agencies and stakeholders. Further, to describe the legislative options available for initiating either a Declared Public Precinct (DPP) or a permanent Dry Zone. Finally, to seek endorsement for pursuit of a DPP.

Councillor - Katriona Kinsella entered the meeting at 9.10 PM.

General Declaration of Interest
Councillor - Katriona Kinsella declared a general conflict of interest pursuant to Section 75B of the Local Government Act for Item 6.1. The nature of Councillor - Katriona Kinsella's general conflict is that she is an employee of DHS which is referenced as involved in the service response to the matter of interest (noting she is not personally involved in that response). Councillor - Katriona Kinsella dealt with the conflict of interest in the following transparent and accountable way by remaining in the room, sitting with staff for the duration of Item 6.1 and not participating in the debate or vote.

Moved: Councillor Alice Campbell
Seconded: Councillor Tom Scheffler

Motion

  1. That Council acknowledges the City of Charles Sturt’s holistic response to anti-social behaviour at the Ovingham Underpass/Karrarendi Yerta Kadla, through collaboration with SAPOL, the City of Prospect, government agencies, community services, residents and businesses to support a wrap-around, community development approach focused on sustainable outcomes.

  2. That Council advocates for the establishment of a Declared Public Precinct (DPP) as a temporary and reviewable mechanism that provides SAPOL with enhanced enforcement powers while balancing the complexity of the issues, ensuring respectful and considered engagement, and protecting the safety and wellbeing of all parties.

  3. That Council staff continue to provide Elected Member and local community updates on the immediate measures, stakeholder collaborations, and advocacy efforts underway, to ensure transparency and accountability in delivering both short-term responses and long-term sustainable outcomes.

Lost

Moved: Councillor Nicole Mazeika
Seconded: Councillor Senthil Chidambaranathan

Motion

  1. That Council acknowledges the City of Charles Sturt’s holistic response to anti-social behaviour at the Ovingham Underpass/Karrarendi Yerta Kadla, through collaboration with SAPOL, the City of Prospect, government agencies, community services, residents and businesses to support a wrap-around, community development approach focused on sustainable outcomes.

  2. That Council advocates for the establishment of a Declared Public Precinct (DPP) as a temporary and reviewable mechanism that provides SAPOL with enhanced enforcement powers while balancing the complexity of the issues, ensuring respectful and considered engagement, and protecting the safety and wellbeing of all parties.

  3. That Council staff continue to provide Elected Member and local community updates on the immediate measures, stakeholder collaborations, and advocacy efforts underway, to ensure transparency and accountability in delivering both short-term responses and long-term sustainable outcomes.

  4. That Council concurrently applies to establish a dry zone at the Ovingham Underpass/Karrarendi Yerta Kadla.
Carried Unanimously

The City of Charles Sturt acknowledges and pays respect to the traditional custodians of the land, the Kaurna people of the Adelaide plains. We pay our respect to Elders past, present and emerging. We respect their spiritual beliefs and connections to land which are of continuing importance to the Kaurna people of today. We acknowledge the contributions and important role that Aboriginal people continue to play within our local community in Charles Sturt. We also respect the culture of Aboriginal people visiting from other areas of South Australia and Australia.

Almighty Father from Whom all goodness flows, grant unto us qualities of wisdom justice and tolerance, that we the civic leaders of this community may govern in harmony and concord.

This we ask in Thy name. 

We also remember and give thanks for those, our sons and daughters, who gave their lives for Australia. 

Lest we forget.

A Motion on Notice has been received from Councillor Kenzie van den Nieuwelaar in relation to the recent algal bloom.


Moved: Councillor Kenzie van den Nieuwelaar
Seconded: Councillor Merlindie Fardone

Motion

That Council:

  1. Acknowledges the significant and ongoing impacts of the recent Karenia algal bloom along the City of Charles Sturt’s coastal areas on the marine environment, local economy, and community wellbeing.

  2. Notes that the Karenia algal bloom has resulted in:
    • Large-scale fish kills and marine die-off along the shoreline, creating distressing visual scenes and health concerns.
    • Discolouration of the water, foam and odours affecting the amenity for residents and beachgoers.
    • Major disruptions to beach access, recreational use, and coastal visitation — particularly during the warmer months and school holidays.

  3. Notes that the cost to Council for the clean-up and recovery operations are substantial and unbudgeted with ongoing expenditure likely if blooms persist or reoccur.

  4. Requests a report from Council staff outlining:
    • How the Karenia algal bloom event can be formally recognised and documented in Council’s environmental risk register, climate adaptation strategy, or coastal management plans.
    • Practical ways for local residents and community groups to contribute to the recovery process — including potential for a community clean-up day, local environmental workshops, or educational events.
    • Options for a community-led art or creative project (e.g. public sculpture, mural, interactive installation or digital media piece) to acknowledge the ecological event, promote environmental awareness, and support community healing and resilience.
    • How Council is currently being assisted by the State and Federal Governments with the clean-up and recovery operations.

  5. Continues to regularly inform our community via our communications channels on: 
    • Clean up progress
    • Ways we are supporting our community
    • Opportunities we are pursuing for State and Federal support
    • Ways our community can be involved

Carried Unanimously

A Motion on Notice has been received from Councillor Kelly Thomas to rescind Council's resolution from 22 September 2025 relating to Jubilee Reserve Redevelopment - Community Engagement Approach. 

Further, Councillor Thomas has proposed a new motion that seeks to defer community consultation until all stakeholders are given the opportunity for a workshop; seek clarification from the Federal Government on the renaming of the related funding application; and engage with all Jubilee Reserve stakeholders to identify and understand their respective needs to inform the development of any initial architectural designs and concept plans. 

Leave of the meeting was sought to continue the meeting until all business is concluded. Leave was granted.

Moved: Councillor Kelly ThomasSeconded: Councillor Kenzie van den Nieuwelaar

Motion

  1. That the resolution of Council 22 September 2025 Item 4.1 (as per below) be revoked on the basis that:
  • Social media has revealed significant opposition from Community Stakeholders at this stage.
  • Questions asked could not be answered at the Council Meeting. 
  • Deputations were censored at the Council Meeting.
  • Questions could not be asked of the deputee's.

4.1 JUBILEE RESERVE REDEVELOPMENT - COMMUNITY ENGAGEMENT APPROACH 
Moved: Councillor Nicholas Le Lacheur Seconded: Councillor Nicole Mazeika 

Acknowledging the importance of community participation in sport and recreation, and recognising that the redevelopment of Jubilee Reserve provides an opportunity to deliver accessible, modern facilities for both organised clubs and the broader community, Council: 

1. Endorses the Community Engagement Approach (Appendix 2) with the following minor amendment: 

a. That the following schools are noted as part of the ‘site user’ stakeholder group. 
i. Alberton Primary School, Allenby Gardens Primary School, Brooklyn Park Primary School, Challa Gardens Primary School, Dominican School, Fulham Gardens Primary School, Fulham North Primary School, Grange Primary School, Hendon Primary School, Henley Beach Primary School, Immaculate Heart of Mary School, Kidman Park Primary School, Kilkenny Primary School, Largs Bay School, Lefevre Peninsula Primary School, Lockleys North Primary School, Mount Carmel College, Nailsworth Primary School, Nazareth Catholic College, Ngutu College, North Adelaide Primary School, North Haven School, Our Lady Queen of Peace School, Our Lady of the Visitation School, Paringa Park Primary School, Portside Christian College, Prospect Primary School, Richmond Primary School, Rosary School, Saint Francis School Lockleys, Saint John Bosco School, Saint Joseph's School Hindmarsh, Saint Margaret Mary’s School, Saint Mary's Memorial School Glenelg, Saint Michael's College, Seaton Park Primary School, Star of the Sea School, Tenison Woods Catholic School, Torrensville Primary School, West Beach Primary School, West Lakes Shore School, Westport Primary School, Whitefriars Catholic School 

2. Notes that a further decision report will be presented following community engagement, outlining outcomes and providing recommendations on the draft design prior to submission of a $5,000,000 funding application to the Federal Government’s Major & Local Community Infrastructure Program. 

3. Notes that the subsequent report will also include recommendations on: 
a. Council’s contribution of $1.5 million (including $701,700 already identified); and 
b. a second stage Community Engagement Approach for further consultation. 

Carried

Division called by Councillor - Nicole Mazeika 
Voters For: 
Councillor - Edgar Agius, Councillor - Alice Campbell, Councillor - Senthil Chidambaranathan, Councillor - Stuart Ghent, Councillor - Katriona Kinsella, Councillor - Nicholas Le Lacheur, Councillor - Nicole Mazeika, Councillor - Michael McEwen, Councillor - Peter Ppiros, Councillor - Tom Scheffler, Councillor - Quin Tran, Councillor - George Turelli (12) 

Voters Against: Councillor - Merlindie Fardone, Councillor - Kelly Thomas, Councillor - Kenzie van den Nieuwelaar (3) 

Not Vote: Mayor - Angela Evans (1) 

The Motion to Item 2.2.1 - 4.1 was Carried

2. That Council resolves to:

Defer the implementation of the Community Consultation until all stakeholders are given the opportunity for a workshop jointly to work out what will and won't work for each group.

3. That Council resolves as follows: 

  1. That prior to any community consultation, Council receives formal notification and clarification from the Federal Government regarding the renaming of the funding application from ‘Adelaide Jaguars Women’s Soccer Club Redevelopment’ to 'Redevelopment of Jubilee Reserve’.

  2. That Council formally engages with all stakeholders of Jubilee Reserve in a joint workshop to identify and understand their respective needs, and that this feedback informs the development of any initial architectural designs and concept plans.

  3. That the Council write to the grant administrator to request an extension of the grant submission deadline to 1 March 2026, to allow sufficient time for comprehensive community consultation, ensure alignment with stakeholder expectations, and confirm that the revised project scope aligns with the intent of the funding commitment.

  4. That Councillor Thomas' notes be included in the Minutes.
Lost


Division called by Councillor - Kenzie van den Nieuwelaar

Voters
For:Councillor - Merlindie Fardone, Councillor - Katriona Kinsella, Councillor - Kelly Thomas, Councillor - George Turelli, Councillor - Kenzie van den Nieuwelaar (5)
Against:Councillor - Edgar Agius, Councillor - Alice Campbell, Councillor - Stuart Ghent, Councillor - Nicholas Le Lacheur, Councillor - Nicole Mazeika, Councillor - Michael McEwen, Councillor - Peter Ppiros, Councillor - Quin Tran (8)
Not Vote:Mayor - Angela Evans (1)
The Motion to Item 7.1. was Lost

A Motion on Notice has been received from Councillor Kenzie van den Nieuwelaar in relation to quarry sand on central beaches.


Moved: Councillor Kenzie van den Nieuwelaar
Seconded: Councillor Merlindie Fardone

Motion

  1. That the Mayor writes to the Minister for Climate, Environment and Water, the Deputy Premier, and the Premier, expressing the City’s strong opposition to the continued use of quarry sand for Central Beach replenishment and highlighting its unsuitability and negative impacts.

  2. That the State Government immediately implements Recommendation 2.2 of the Adelaide Beach Management Review, commencing sand recycling via carting of accumulated beach sand from the northern beaches to the Central Beaches as a more appropriate interim solution.
Carried Unanimously

The City of Charles Sturt acknowledges and pays respect to the traditional custodians of the land, the Kaurna people of the Adelaide plains. We pay our respect to Elders past, present and emerging. We respect their spiritual beliefs and connections to land which are of continuing importance to the Kaurna people of today. We acknowledge the contributions and important role that Aboriginal people continue to play within our local community in Charles Sturt. We also respect the culture of Aboriginal people visiting from other areas of South Australia and Australia.

Almighty Father from Whom all goodness flows, grant unto us qualities of wisdom justice and tolerance, that we the civic leaders of this community may govern in harmony and concord.

This we ask in Thy name. 

We also remember and give thanks for those, our sons and daughters, who gave their lives for Australia. 

Lest we forget.


Leave of the meeting was sought in accordance with the Code of Practice for Meeting Procedures to hear the additional four deputations and to bring forward all deputations relating to the Strategic and Engagement Committee meeting Item for Woodville South Traffic Safety Improvements. Leave was granted.

Leave of the meeting was also sought to bring forward and hear first Business Item 6.1 Recognition of the 2025 LGITSA Awards Achievements. Leave was granted.

The Audit and Risk Committee was held on Wednesday, 22 October 2025.


Moved: Councillor Nicholas Le LacheurSeconded: Councillor Stuart Ghent

That having considered the recommendations of the Committee which has read and considered the reports in the agenda related to items:

 

4.1. - ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) UPDATE - PRESENTATION AND REPORT
 
Motion
 
  1. That the presentation and report be received and noted.
  
4.2. - BUSINESS CONTINUITY PLAN - PRESENTATION AND REPORT
 
Motion 
 
  1. That the presentation be received and noted and that the presentation be included within the Minutes of the meeting.
  
4.3. - YEAR END AUDITED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS JUNE 2025
 
Motion
 
  1. That the Committee recommends to Council that the Audited Financial Statements for the year ending 30 June 2025 prepared in accordance with the requirements of the Model Financial Statements be received and noted and that the certification of the financial statements proceed in accordance with Regulation 14 Local Government (Financial Management) Regulations 2011, noting the amendment to "Note 1 -  Summary of Material Accounting Policies" be updated for 2023/24 financial year.
  
4.4. - ANNUAL REPORT AND YEAR END AUDITED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS 2024/25 – CENTRAL ADELAIDE WASTE AND RECYCING AUTHORITY (CAWRA)
 
Motion
 
  1. To present to the Audit and Risk Committee the Annual Report and Audited Financial Statements for the Central Adelaide Waste and Recycling Authority (CAWRA) to be endorsed and included as part of the City of Charles Sturt's Annual Report 2024/25.
 
4.5. - AUDIT AND RISK COMMITTEE 2025 WORKPLAN UPDATE AND DRAFT 2026 WORKPLAN
 
Motion 
 
 That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That progress against the 2025 Audit and Risk Committee Workplan be noted.
  2. That the 2026 Audit and Risk Committee Workplan be accepted.
 
4.6. - DRAFT INTERNAL AUDIT PLAN FY26-FY28
 
Motion 
 
  1. That the Committee recommends to Council that the proposed Draft Internal Audit Plan FY26-FY28 (Appendix 1) is endorsed.
 
4.7. - STATUS UPDATE FOR ALL OUTSTANDING INTERNAL AUDIT ACTIONS
 
Motion 
 
  1. That the report be received and noted.
 
4.8. - CEO ANNUAL REPORT ON INTERNAL AUDIT PROCESS 
 
Motion 
 
  1. That the Audit and Risk Committee notes the CEO Annual Report on Council's Internal Audit processes for 2024/25.
 
4.9. - QUARTERLY RISK UPDATE
 
Motion 
 
  1. That the report be received and noted.
 
4.10. - ANNUAL AUDIT AND RISK COMMITTEE PERFORMANCE REVIEW 2024/25 RESULTS
 
Motion 
 
 That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That the 2025 Annual Audit and Risk Committee Performance Review findings are accepted by the Committee.
  2. That the Committee notes that there were no recommended amendments to be made to the Terms of Reference for the Audit and Risk Committee.
 
4.11. - AUDIT AND RISK COMMITTEE ANNUAL REPORT TO COUNCIL
 
Motion 
 
  1. That the Audit and Risk Committee endorses the attached Annual Report as an accurate representation of its activities for the 2024/25 financial year, for presentation to Council and inclusion in Council's Annual Report for the same period.
  
9.1. - PRESENTATION - CYBER SECURITY UPDATE
 
Motion 
 
 That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That Council notes the risks and mitigation strategies that are being undertaken to address the cyber security risks.
 
9.2. - CONFIDENTIAL SESSION – AUDIT AND RISK COMMITTEE AND COUNCIL AUDITORS
 
Motion 

  1. That the following comments were discussed during the confidential session with Council’s internal and external auditors and require the General Manager Corporate Services to consider if the following can be enacted:
    • That the Quarterly budget reviews are provided to the Audit and Risk Committee for review at their meetings as soon as reasonably practicable and ideally prior to presentation at the corporate services meeting. 
    • That the original budget versus end of year outcome report be tabled at the final Audit and Risk Committee for each calendar year along with the financial statement reports.   
    • That the Audit and Risk Committee recommend that a fifth meeting is scheduled to focus on the Audited Financial Statement and the statutory requirement to liaise with Council’s auditors on a confidential basis once per year.

  2. That the Committee acknowledges that the 5-year terms Council external Auditors – Galpins has been completed and the Committee thanks Galpins for their 5-years of service and support.

  

Council adopts the recommendations of the Committee as printed in the Minutes of this Committee.

Carried Unanimously

The Strategic and Engagement Committee was held on Monday, 20 October 2025.


Moved: Councillor Nicole Mazeika
Seconded: Councillor Nicholas Le Lacheur

That having considered the recommendations of the Committee which has read and considered the reports in the agenda related to all items with the exception of Item 4.2:

 

3.1. - DEPUTATION - LIME GREEN FESTIVAL PROPOSAL
 
Motion
 
  1. That the deputation be received and noted. 
 
  1. That Mr Matthew Wright-Simon be thanked for his presentation and any notes that comply with Council's Code of Practice for Meeting Procedures and the laws of defamation, be included in the Minutes.
 
3.2. - DEPUTATION - INSTALLATION OF SPEED HUMPS ALONG GLEN STREETS WOODVILLE SOUTH
 
Motion
 
  1. That the deputation be received and noted. 
 
  1. That Mr Tony Francesca be thanked for his presentation and any notes that comply with Council's Code of Practice for Meeting Procedures and the laws of defamation, be included in the Minutes.
 
3.3. - DEPUTATION - INSTALLATION OF SPEED HUMPS ON GLENGARRY STREET
 
Motion
 
  1. That the deputation be received and noted. 
 
  1. That Mr Nicholas Frangiskos be thanked for his presentation and any notes that comply with Council's Code of Practice for Meeting Procedures and the laws of defamation, be included in the Minutes.
 
3.4. - DEPUTATION - CONCERNS ABOUT HIGH TRAFFIC VOLUMES AND SPEEDING ON OVAL AVENUE
 
Motion
 
  1. That the deputation be received and noted. 
 
  1. That Mr Callum Davies be thanked for his presentation and any notes that comply with Council's Code of Practice for Meeting Procedures and the laws of defamation, be included in the Minutes.
  
4.1. - PRESENTATION - UPDATE ON AVOID FRAILTY PROJECT
 
Motion  
   
  1. That the presentation be received and noted.
 
  1. That Professor Renuka Visanathan from The University of Adelaide be thanked for the presentation and a copy be included in the Minutes.
 
4.3. - WOODVILLE TOWN HALL 2027 CENTENARY UPGRADE REPORT AND PRESENTATION
 
Motion
 
 That in recognition of the Centenary of Woodville Town Hall in 2027, and to celebrate its civic, cultural and architectural significance, that the Committee recommends to Council:
 
  1. Endorse the inclusion in the draft 2026/27 budget a Capital Project budget bid of $1,448,000 for sound, lighting and venue upgrade works prior to Woodville Town Hall’s Centenary year in 2027.
 
  1. Endorse the inclusion in the draft 2026/27 budget an Annual Operating budget bid of $150,000 to establish a programming fund to underwrite and attract high-quality events.
 
  1. Endorse the inclusion in the draft 2026/27 budget an Annual Operating Budget bid of $35,000 to resource additional operational capacity of 0.4 FTE for Woodville Town Hall.
 
  1. Note that the above bids, if approved, will be incorporated into Council’s Long-Term Financial Plan and Asset Management Plans at the next scheduled review in accordance with the statutory review cycle.
 
  1. That the $109,971.81 currently included in the Council Buildings Asset Management Plan for 2028/29 be brought forward to 2026/27 to enable important renewal works to be completed prior to the Woodville Town Hall’s Centenary in 2027.
 
  1. That Council receives a report in late 2027 evaluating the performance of the programming fund and overall activation outcomes.
 
  1. Write to Minister of Arts enquiring about a state government contribution to the Woodville Townhall upgrade.
 
  1. That staff be thanked for their presentation.  
  
4.4. - EVENT GRANTS & EVENT SPONSORSHIP: REQUESTS FOR FUNDING
 
Motion
 
  1. That Council approves the following events for funding from the Community Event Fund:
  • Australian Melanoma Research Foundation - Melanoma March
  • Bulgarians’ Educational and Friendly Society - Zdravei Bulgarian Festival
  • Greek Orthodox Community of South Australia Incorporated - Blessing of the Waters
  • Woodville Concert Band - Music With Motion Down Under
 
  1. That Council approves the following events for funding as Event Grants: 
  • Adelaide Fringe 2026 - Drum & Bass on the Bike
  • Horsepower Crew - Summertime Motor Meet
  • POP Events Adelaide - Christmas Twilight Markets
  • Rowing South Australia Inc - 2026 South Australian Rowing Championship
  • South Australian Athletic League Inc - The Wester Athletic Club Gift
  • TQ Productions - Alma Brazil! Festival
  • We Rally Creative - 2026 Bowden Fringe
 
  1.  That Council note the updates for the following events that are in their third year of a previously endorsed funding agreement
  • Rotary Club of West Lakes - Christmas Fun for Kids
  • Shapeshifter Brewing - Westfest
  • St Clair Community Events - Carols by Candlelight
  • Telugu Association - Deepavali
  • Tennyson Dunes - Tennyson Dunes Open Day
  • West Beach SLSC - Pink and Blue Event
  
4.5. - DISCHARGE OF ENCUMBRANCE - 45 MARLBOROUGH STREET, FULHAM GARDENS
 
Motion
 
That the Strategic and Engagement Committee recommends to Council:
 
  1. That Council acknowledge there is no further need for the encumbrance (Document No. 3713058) as noted on Certificate of Title Volume 5740 Folio 678 and shown in Appendix 1.
 
  1. That Council consent to discharge the encumbrance shown at Appendix 1 for nil consideration, pursuant to Section 143(1) of the Real Property Act 1886.
 
  1. That Council grant the Mayor and CEO authority to sign any document or act in any conveyancing matter to discharge the encumbrance noted as Document No. 3713058 and to deliver this resolution.
 
4.6. - HIGH PRODUCTIVITY VEHICLE NETWORK/GREATER ADELAIDE FREIGHT BYPASS
 
Motion
 
 That the Strategic and Engagement Committee recommends to Council:
 
  1. That Council notes the request from the City of Burnside for the State Government to match Federal Government funding for the High Productivity Vehicle Network / Greater Adelaide Freight Bypass in South Australia.
 
  1. That Council endorses the Mayor and Chief Executive Officer to sign the joint advocacy letter supporting the High Productivity Vehicle Network / Greater Adelaide Freight Bypass.

  

Council adopts the recommendations of the Committee as printed in the Minutes of this Committee.

Carried Unanimously

4.2. - WOODVILLE SOUTH TRAFFIC SAFETY IMPROVEMENTS - OUTCOMES OF CONSULTATION

Moved: Councillor Nicole Mazeika
Seconded: Councillor Kelly Thomas

Motion
  
 That the Committee recommends that Council:
  
  1. Notes the outcomes of Community Engagement as summarised in Appendix 1.
 
  1. Extends the consultation period to allow for additional engagement on alternative traffic calming treatments, and includes Oval Avenue and Connor Avenue. The engagement process will comprise:
  • An initial stage, including a drop-in session with community members to assist staff in identifying viable traffic calming options; and
  • A subsequent four-week community consultation period to seek feedback and understand community preferences for the identified options.
 
  1. Notes that residents have been encouraged to contact Council staff to discuss eligibility for parking time limit exemptions and driveway access support. 
 
  1. That the Mayor write a further letter on behalf of Council to the Hon Chris Picton MP, Minister for Health and Wellbeing, requesting an urgent and comprehensive review of car parking facilities at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital, with the aim of identifying and delivering additional parking for hospital staff, including options to reduce the cost of parking for QEH staff, and emphasising the need to support staff safety and uphold the organisation's duty of care.
Carried Unanimously

The Operations Committee was held on Monday, 20 October 2025.


Moved: Councillor Alice CampbellSeconded: Councillor Edgar Agius

That having considered the recommendations of the Committee which has read and considered the reports in the agenda related to all items with the exception of 4.2:

 

4.1. - GRANT ACCEPTANCE FROM THE STATE GOVERNMENT FOR WATER EFFICIENCY
 
Motion
 
That the Committee recommends to the Council: 
 
  1. That Council accepts $4,056,141 (ex GST) for capital works associated with alternative water delivery across the City.
 
  1. That Council notes the funding is provided in accordance with the final Funding Deed between the Minister for Climate, Environment and Water and Council.
 
  1. That Council authorises the Chief Executive Officer to execute the funding Deed and affix the Common Seal of Council to the deed.
 

4.3. - LOCAL CENTRES REVITALISATION INTIATIVE - PROJECT UPDATE AND OPPORTUNITIES
 
Motion
 
That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That Council notes that the Local Centre Revitalisation project at Athol Park will be integrated into the Your Neighbourhood Plan flagship initiative Area B project.
 
  1. That Council endorses the use of surplus funds from the Athol Park Local Centre to be applied to support a Local Centre initiative at Ovingham.
 
  1. That a Master Plan be developed for the Kilkenny Local Activity Centre and Wilpena Terrace, enabling the coordination and integration of current and future local project opportunities within the Local Centre Revitalisation flagship initiative.
 
  1. That the following variations to the Capital Works Program be approved and adjusted in the budget and annual financial statements 2025/26 as a transfer between renewal and new/upgrade works: 
  1.  Budgeted expenditure for David Terrace Local Activity Centres Kilkenny, (Project 3421 ‐ Upgrade) be increased by $21,871 from savings in Road Reconstruction Program 2025/26 - Design Allowance (Project 3725 ‐ Renewal) to undertake a master plan for the project. 

  1. That the following variations to the Capital Works Program be approved and budgets or scope adjusted accordingly:
         b. Budgeted expenditure for Alicia Street Athol Park Local Centre (Project 3582 ‐ Upgrade) of $5,000 be reallocated to undertake Consultation and identify placemaking opportunities for the Ovingham Overpass Local                   Centre. 

  1. That by endorsing the variations listed in 4 and 5 above, Council is endorsing a variation to the approved Asset Management Plan renewal schedule where relevant.

 

Council adopts the recommendations of the Committee as printed in the Minutes of this Committee.

Carried Unanimously

Material Declaration of Interest

Councillor - Alice Campbell declared a material conflict of interest pursuant to Section 75C of the Local Government Act for Item 2.2.3-4.2. The nature of Councillor - Alice Campbell's material conflict is that the recommendation mentions SANFL and her partner is an employee of SANFL and left the meeting.

Councillor - Alice Campbell left the meeting at 7.50 PM

Moved: Councillor Edgar AgiusSeconded: Councillor Stuart Ghent

4.2. - CITY OPERATIONS CAPITAL WORKS & OPERATING PROGRAM VARIATIONS
 
Motion
 
That the Committee recommends to the Council: 
 
  1. That the following variations to the Capital Works Program or Annual Operating Program be approved and adjusted in the Financial Statements at the next quarterly review as they involve transfers between renewal and new/upgrade works and or new projects to be funded by unbudgeted income:-
 
  1. Budgeted expenditure for Football Park New Open Space (Project 3682 - New) be increased by $250,000 from external funding sourced to deliver the works.  

  1.  That the following variations to the Capital Works Program be approved and budgets or scope adjusted accordingly:
  1. Budgeted expenditure for Stormwater - Drain Renewal Program 2024/25 (WIP) (Project 3576 - Renewal) be increased by $25,000 from savings in Road Rehabilitation Program 2025/26 - K&G Renewal 2025/26 (Project 3712 - Renewal). 
  2. Budgeted expenditure for Road Rehabilitation Program of Works 2024/25 (Project 3555 - Renewal) be increased by $311,000 from savings in Road Reconstruction Program 2025/26 - Contingency (Project 3724 - Renewal).  

  1. That by endorsing the variations listed in 1. above, Council is endorsing a variation to the approved Asset Management Plan renewal schedule where relevant.
Carried Unanimously

The purpose of this report is to acknowledge and celebrate the City of Charles Sturt’s success and recognition at the 2025 Local Government Information Technology South Australia (LGITSA) Achievement Awards. The City received two awards, the Culture Shifter Award and the Information Technology Innovation Award, and was also shortlisted in three additional categories. These achievements highlight the City’s leadership, innovation and collaboration to deliver services for our community. 


Moved: Councillor Tom Scheffler
Seconded: Councillor Michael McEwen

  1. That Council acknowledges and congratulates Anita Hulm, Senior Business Analyst, on receiving the Culture Shifter Award.

  2. That Council acknowledges and congratulates the following staff on receiving the Information Technology Innovation Award for the Customer Relationship Management Transformation Project:

         Kristie Johnson, General Manager Engaged Community
         Kristy Noakes, Manager Community Engagement and Experience
         Georgia Borthwick, Customer Experience Advocate
         Kerri Cooper, Coordinator IT Projects
         Anita Hulm, Senior Business Analyst
         Michelle Swan, Customer Experience Lead
         Marc O'Conaill, Coordinator IT Architecture
         Simon Armitage, Manager Financial Services

To inform Council of the Federal Government’s aged care reforms, including the introduction of the new Aged Care Act (November 2025) and the Support at Home program (replacing Commonwealth Home Support Program nationally from 1 July 2027). This report provides Council with the outcome of the Electoral Commission of South Australia’s (ECSA) decision to grant an exemption certificate, allowing retention of the current Council composition as part of the Representation Review process.


Moved: Councillor George Turelli
Seconded: Councillor Tom Scheffler

Motion

  1. That Council acknowledges that an exemption certificate has been provided by the Electoral Commission of South Australia to maintain the current structure of Council, that being:
    • the Principal Member of the Council continues to be a Mayor, elected by the Council area as a whole;
    • Council will maintain an eight Ward structure, subject to the required boundary re-alignment with Grange Ward to ensure Semaphore Park Ward is brought within the quota tolerances;
    • each of the eight Wards retain their current names; and
    • the elected body of Council continue to comprise of a total of 16 Ward Councillors, with two Councillors elected from each ward.

  2. That Council acknowledges that these representation arrangements will be effective from the periodic election in November 2026.

Carried Unanimously

Questions on Notices have been received from Councillor Nicole Mazeika in relation to ongoing delays and missed rubbish collections across the City of Charles Sturt.

Questions and Answers

Service Accountability

  1. What actions is Council currently taking to ensure Cleanaway meets agreed collection deadlines under the current contract?
Council has been proactively working with Cleanaway to address service delivery issues for a number of years. These measures include monthly KPI monitoring and review meetings with Cleanaway staff to discuss and drive contract performance improvements. In May 2024, due to a further deterioration in performance, Council issued Cleanaway the first Notice of Direction (Default Notice) under the contract that implemented financial performance penalties for failing to meet the bin collection KPI's.  Cleanaway are required to ensure missed bin collections are kept below 0.1% and when missed bin collections exceed 0.1% a financial penalty is applied in the form of an invoice credit the following month. In January 2025 a second Notice of Direction (Default Notice) was issued due to continued failure to return to empty missed bins within a reasonable timeframe. This second Notice of Direction allowed Council to get a third party (either Council staff or another contractor) to empty the missed bins and charge any incurred costs back to Cleanaway.  This Notice of Direction has been enacted on a number of occasions in 2025. 

These interventions by Council were effective (initially) with a period of improved performance by Cleanaway the first half of 2025. Unfortunately, Cleanaway's performance has declined again sharply in recent months, so further efforts are now required.  CAWRA wrote to Cleanaway on Monday 20 October 2025 to urgently draw their attention to these matters and (among other things) request that Cleanaway provide a plan of action to restore performance. As a result, a meeting took place between senior staff of Council, CAWRA and Cleanaway on Wednesday 22 October 2025 at which Cleanaway has committed to a number of actions, one of which is to bring in a third-party waste collection contractor to complete collection runs that Cleanaway don't have the capacity to complete at this point in time.  This will significantly reduce, if not eliminate, the large number of delayed and missed collections experienced daily at present. Further details on this and other measures being implemented by Cleanaway will be provided to Council at the Council Workshop on the 27th of October.

  1. How is service performance being monitored and reported back to Council?
Monthly contract performance meetings monitor performance against contract KPI's. Where Cleanaway are aware of an impending bin collection issue due to a lack of drivers or trucks and collection runs won't be completed on the scheduled day, these are required to be reported to Council staff in the morning of that day.

Penalties and Financial Management

  1. Are penalties or fines issued to Cleanaway for not meeting service standards or contractual obligations?
Yes, financial penalties are issued to Cleanaway for not meeting contract KPI's. It should also be noted that there are financial bonuses as part of the performance management mechanism to reward high performance that is better than the missed bin KPI (less than 0.049% missed bins), however Cleanaway haven’t managed to achieve a performance bonus yet.

  1. How will council use this monies raised from performance penalties? Will this go to operational costs or back into the budget bottom line?
The performance penalties are financial credits against the monthly invoice. Financially, this sits as an underspend (or budget saving) vs the residential waste collection budget on the Council P&L.

Operational Impact on Council and the Community

  1. Has Council had to deploy its own resources or staff to complete missed bin collections?
Yes, the City Clean team that usually collect public litter bins (reserve and street litter bins) have been deployed to collect missed bins that have remained uncollected for over 3 days.

  1. If so, what has been the total cost of this intervention to the community?
No cost to the community as the cost is recovered from Cleanaway via an invoice or as a credit against our monthly invoice, however it can be an interruption to normal service delivery for the City Clean team.

Future Contract and Market Options

  1. When is the current Cleanaway contract due to expire or be reviewed?
The current contract expires in April 2028 but has an extension clause that allows Council to extend the contract at Council's sole discretion for another 3 years to 2031.  CAWRA is currently collating detail regarding the current contract performance, any commercial considerations and implications of the current contract for Council and Cleanaway, and considerations regarding any potential contract extension, which will be presented to Council in a confidential report. 

  1. What alternative waste collection providers are available in the market that Council could consider?
There are a number of residential kerbside waste and recycling collection contractors, and these include companies such as Solo and Veolia.

The City of Charles Sturt acknowledges and pays respect to the traditional custodians of the land, the Kaurna people of the Adelaide plains. We pay our respect to Elders past, present and emerging. We respect their spiritual beliefs and connections to land which are of continuing importance to the Kaurna people of today. We acknowledge the contributions and important role that Aboriginal people continue to play within our local community in Charles Sturt. We also respect the culture of Aboriginal people visiting from other areas of South Australia and Australia.

Almighty Father from Whom all goodness flows, grant unto us qualities of wisdom justice and tolerance, that we the civic leaders of this community may govern in harmony and concord.

This we ask in Thy name. 

We also remember and give thanks for those, our sons and daughters, who gave their lives for Australia. 

Lest we forget.
