This report summarises the community feedback that is shaping the Preliminary Master Plan Concept and the forthcoming Draft Concept Design for Jubilee Reserve.

These insights, together with the Federal Government’s $5\u202Fmillion commitment to deliver a permanent home for the Adelaide Jaguars Women’s Soccer Club, have informed the development of the four scenarios considered in this report, with Scenario\u202F3 emerging as the preferred option for Council endorsement and the basis for the MLCIP funding application.

General Declaration of Interest
Councillor - Senthil Chidambaranathan declared a general conflict of interest pursuant to Section 75B of the Local Government Act for Item 6.1. The nature of Councillor - Senthil Chidambaranathan's general conflict is due to his candidacy in the forthcoming State Legislative Council election. Councillor - Senthil Chidambaranathan dealt with the conflict of interest in the following transparent and accountable way and remaining in the room, sitting with staff for the duration of Item 6.1 and not participating in the debate or vote.

General Declaration of Interest
Councillor - Merlindie Fardone declared a general conflict of interest pursuant to Section 75B of the Local Government Act for Item 6.1. The nature of Councillor Merlindie Fardone's general conflict is due to her candidacy as part of the upcoming State Election. Councillor - Merlindie Fardone dealt with the conflict of interest in the following transparent and accountable way and remaining in the room, sitting with staff for the duration of Item 6.1 and not participating in the debate or vote.

Councillor - Nicole Mazeika left the meeting at 10:01 PM.
Councillor - Nicole Mazeika entered the meeting at 10:05 PM.

Moved: Councillor Nicholas Le Lacheur

Motion

That Council:
 
  1. Thank staff for the presentation and that a copy of the presentation be included in the Minutes.

  2. Receives and notes the Community Engagement Summary Report as detailed in Appendix 1.  

  3. Receives and notes the four Scenario Master Plan Concepts as detailed in Appendix 2. 

  4. Endorse Scenario 3 (revised) (Appendix 2 - page20), as the preferred Master Plan Concept for the Jubilee Reserve Redevelopment for further engagement in accordance with the Community Engagement Approach Stage 2 (Appendix 3). 

  5. Authorises the CEO to prepare and lodge a funding application to the Federal Government’s Major & Local Community Infrastructure Program consistent with: 
    1. Scenario 3 (revised); and
    2. The $5 million Federal election commitment from the Hon Mark Butler MP to create a permanent home for the Adelaide Jaguars Women’s Soccer Club at Jubilee Reserve, including provision for a dedicated full-sized senior soccer pitch with perimeter fencing compliant with Women’s National Premier League (WNPL) standards, upgraded and additional sports lighting, female-friendly change rooms, and enhanced clubroom and community amenities.

  6. Notes that a $701,700 Council contribution toward the redevelopment has previously been endorsed and approves the inclusion of an additional $800,000 toward the redevelopment in the 2025/26 financial year.

  7. Notes the petition titled “Petition – Opposition to fences at Jubilee Reserve,” received on 23 February 2026 (Item 5.2), and recommends that it be included and considered as part of Stage Two engagement, with outcomes reported in the subsequent Stage Two Consultation Report.

  8. That the scope is expanded to include lighting in the Bartley Terrace tunnel and West Lakes Sports Club oval.

  9. That the parties work toward Adelaide Jaguars integration with the current Club West Lakes governance model as an affiliated member.

  10. That commitment is given to the community for main pitch access outside of game and training times.

Councillor - Alice Campbell left the meeting at 10:27 PM.

Councillor - Alice Campbell entered the meeting at 10:29 PM.

Seconded: Councillor Stuart Ghent


Moved: Councillor Stuart Ghent
Seconded: Councillor Michael McEwen

Adjournment 11:20 PM

That Council continue the consideration of Item 6.1 and the take a 10 minute break in accordance with the Code of Practice for Meeting Procedures following Item 6.1.
Carried Unanimously


The Motion to Item 6.1 was Carried 

Division called by Councillor - Nicole Mazeika

Voters
For:Councillor - Edgar Agius, Councillor - Alice Campbell, Councillor - Merlindie Fardone, Councillor - Stuart Ghent, Councillor - Katriona Kinsella, Councillor - Nicholas Le Lacheur, Councillor - Nicole Mazeika, Councillor - Michael McEwen, Councillor - Peter Ppiros, Councillor - Tom Scheffler, Councillor - Quin Tran, Councillor - Rachele Tullio (12)
Against:Councillor - Kelly Thomas, Councillor - Kenzie van den Nieuwelaar (2)
Not Vote:Mayor - Angela Evans (1)
The Motion to Item 6.1. was Carried




















Moved: Councillor Michael McEwen
Seconded: Councillor Edgar Agius

Resumption - 11.31 PM

That Council resume.


Carried Unanimously

At the resumption of the meeting Councillor - Merlindie Fardone was not present.

Councillor - Merlindie Fardone entered the meeting at 11:33 PM.

Moved: Councillor Michael McEwen
Seconded: Councillor Edgar Agius

Motion

  1. That Council hear Item 4.7, Item 11.2 and Item 12.1.

  2. That all other items are deferred to the Council meeting on 10 March 2026 with the exception of Item 11.1 which will be deferred to the Council meeting of 23 March 2026.
Carried

This report provides Council with an updated position on a number of concurrently occurring land transaction matters. Including: Compulsory acquisition of Council Land at 67 -85 Woodville Rd by Dept Infrastructure and Transport (DIT); the purchase of land at William St Beverley for additional Open Space from Dept Infrastructure and Transport (DIT); and the Grange Bowling Club Unsolicited Proposal following member votes on the proposed amalgamation with the West Lakes Bowling Club. While Grange Bowling Club members voted in favour of progressing Council’s formal offer, West Lakes Bowling Club members resolved not to proceed. As a result, the amalgamation pathway will not progress in its current form.

 

The report seeks Council direction on a revised pathway to progress the proposed acquisition and redevelopment of the Grange Bowling Club site. The total proposed Council financial commitment and prudential framework previously considered by Council remain unchanged.

 

This report is presented in confidence pursuant to Section 90(3)(b) of the Local Government Act 1999 as it contains information the disclosure of which could reasonably be expected to confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting, or proposing to conduct, business, or to prejudice the commercial position of the council; and would, on balance, be contrary to the public interest.

9.1 Authorise the Chief Executive Officer to issue a revised formal offer to the Grange Bowling Club consistent with the Revised Detailed Proposal attached as Appendix 1, reflecting:

  • acquisition of the site at 11 Wilson Court, Grange for $1.5 million;
  • redevelopment within the $4.2 million capital allocation;
  • a total Council commitment of $5.7 million (excluding GST);
  • a peppercorn lease of up to 42 years; and
  • inclusion of a structured Expressions of Interest process.

The Strategic and Engagement Committee was held on Monday, 16 February 2026 and considered Item 9.1 - Presentation: Social Infrastructure & Land Acquisition Opportunities: Brompton & Bowden. The brief of this item is provided as follows:

The report is provided for information and discussion only, to support Committee awareness of strategic context and potential future considerations.

In accordance with the Local Government Act 1999 the CEO is recommending that this report be heard in confidence under Section 90(3)(b) as it contains information the disclosure of which (i) could reasonably be expected to confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting, or proposing to conduct, business, or to prejudice the commercial position of the council; and (ii) would, on balance, be contrary to the public interest.


Moved: Councillor Nicholas Le Lacheur
Seconded: Councillor Nicole Mazeika

Motion

  1. That having considered the recommendation of the Committee which has read and considered the report in the agenda related to item:

    9.1 PRESENTATION: SOCIAL INFRASTRUCTURE & LAND ACQUISITION OPPORTUNITIES: BROMPTON & BOWDEN
     
    Motion

    1. Confidential Motion.

    2. That Item 9.1 Social Infrastructure & Land Acquisition Opportunities: Brompton & Bowden having been considered in confidence pursuant to section 90(3)(b) of the Local Government Act 1999, the Council hereby orders, in accordance with section 91(7) of the Local Government Act 1999, that the report and the minutes relating to this item be kept confidential until such time as the relevant land-related matters have progressed to a stage where disclosure would no longer prejudice the commercial position of the Council, or for a period of 3 years which every is the earlier.

Deputation Refusal 
In accordance with the Local Government (Procedures at Meeting) Regulations I’m required to provide the Council with my decision to decline a deputation. I received a deputation request from Lester Mackenzie and Neil Comben on behalf of the Grange Bowling Club for the meeting tonight on Item 6.3 - Disability Access and Inclusion Plan 2026-2030.
 
The Council Code of Practice for Meeting Procedures state that a deputation request for an item that is listed on the agenda is to be received by 10am on the day of the meeting and the request was received by staff at 10:03am. Therefore decline the request as it was received outside of the nominated time. 
 
As the members are aware you have the ability to move motion to overrule my decision and allow Lester Mackenzie and Neil Comben to speak if they are in the gallery tonight.

Moved: Councillor Rachele TullioSeconded: Councillor George Turelli

Motion

That the Mayor's decision to decline the deputation request from Mr Lester Mackenzie and Mr Neil Comben is overruled, allowing the deputation to be heard.
Carried Unanimously


Moved: Councillor Rachele TullioSeconded: Councillor Quin Tran

Motion

  1. That the deputation be received and noted. 

  2. That Mr Lester Mackenzie and Mr Neil Comben be thanked for their presentation and any notes that comply with Council's Code of Practice for Meeting Procedures and the laws of defamation, be included in the Minutes.
Carried Unanimously

The City of Charles Sturt acknowledges and pays respect to the traditional custodians of the land, the Kaurna people of the Adelaide plains. We pay our respect to Elders past, present and emerging. We respect their spiritual beliefs and connections to land which are of continuing importance to the Kaurna people of today. We acknowledge the contributions and important role that Aboriginal people continue to play within our local community in Charles Sturt. We also respect the culture of Aboriginal people visiting from other areas of South Australia and Australia.

Almighty Father from Whom all goodness flows, grant unto us qualities of wisdom justice and tolerance, that we the civic leaders of this community may govern in harmony and concord.

This we ask in Thy name. 

We also remember and give thanks for those, our sons and daughters, who gave their lives for Australia. 

Lest we forget. 

Councillor - Katriona Kinsella entered the meeting at 7:02 PM.

The Audit and Risk Committee was held on Wednesday, 25 February 2026.


Moved: Councillor Nicholas Le Lacheur
Seconded: Councillor Michael McEwen

That having considered the recommendations of the Committee which has read and considered the reports in the agenda related to items:

 

4.1 AUDIT AND RISK COMMITTEE 2026 WORKPLAN UPDATE


Motion 
 
That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That the revised 2026 Audit and Risk Committee Workplan, and progress against the Workplan be received and noted.
 
4.2 PRESENTATION AND REPORT - REVIEW OF LONG TERM FINANCIAL PLAN, ASSUMPTIONS AND BUDGET DEVELOPMENT 2026/27

Motion 
 
That the Committee recommends to the Corporate Services Committee:
 
  1. That the report be received and noted.
 
  1. That the information contained in the report be considered in formulating a recommendation to the Corporate Services Committee and Council on the Long Term Financial Plan parameters 2026/27, to guide the preparation of the Draft 2026/27 budget.
 
  1. That the assumptions detailed in Appendix 1 be endorsed, specifically:
 
  1. that the Deloittee Access Economics forecast CPI of 3.71% is used as the basis for the LTFP
  2. the Property Growth assumption is 1.1%
  3. that salaries budget is based on the Wages Price Index of 3.2%
  4. that the Long Term Financial Plan provide for a debt level at Year 10 of up to 20% of Year 1 rates revenue within the LTFP model. 
  5. the LTFP assumes asset values will grow with CPI, and in between full valuations Council applies an indexation to the replacement cost using the Australian Bureau of Statistics Construction Industry Price
 
  1. That a further report on implementing differential rating for short term rentals be presented to the Corporate Services Committee and Council for consideration as part of the Draft budget 2026/27.   
 
  1. That the following feedback be provided to the Corporate Services Committee for consideration:
  1. Include the dollar value in the Operating Surplus for each scenario in presentation for Corporate Services Committee.
  2. Table 3 in Appendix 1 - Expanding table on assumptions on indices that significantly increase above CPI.
  3. Include that all scenarios we have capacity to deliver.
  4. Add commentary in the assumptions regarding savings and productivity targets and the stability of FTE.

4.3 QUARTERLY BUDGET REVIEW - DECEMBER 2025

Motion 
 
That the Committee recommends to the Corporate Services Committee:
 
  1. That the report be received and noted.
  2. That the 2025/26 Budget be amended to recognise the additional income received to date, together with the associated expenditure as detailed in Appendix 1 to this report.
  3. That the revised Budgeted Annual Financial Statements as detailed in Appendix 2 which have been recast to include the impact of the December Q2 budget Review are adopted.
  4. That the Committee provide the following feedback to the Corporate Services Committee for consideration.
    1. Nil

4.4 END OF QUARTER FINANCIAL REPORT - DECEMBER 2025

Motion
 
That the Committee recommends to the Corporate Services Committee:
 
  1. That the report be received and noted.
 
  1. That the Committee provide the following feedback to the Corporate Services Committee for consideration.
  1. That the Executive Management Team consider a forecast figure for WIP to be presented at the next Audit and Risk Committee meeting. 
 
4.5 QUARTERLY RISK UPDATE

Motion
 
  1. That the report be received and noted.

4.6 INTERNAL AUDIT WORKPLAN STATUS UPDATE

Motion

  1. That the report be received and noted.

9.1 PRESENTATION AND REPORT - ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE (AI) UPDATE

 

Motion
 
  1. That the presentation and report be received and noted.

Council adopts the recommendations of the Committee as printed in the Minutes of this Committee.

Carried Unanimously

The Corporate Services Committee was held on Monday, 2 March 2026.

Councillor - Alice Campbell ​left the meeting at 7:10 PM.

Moved: Councillor Michael McEwen
Seconded: Councillor Peter Ppiros

That having considered the recommendations of the Committee which has read and considered the reports in the agenda related to items:

 

4.1 PRESENTATION AND REPORT - REVIEW OF LONG TERM FINANCIAL PLAN, ASSUMPTIONS AND BUDGET DEVELOPMENT 2026/27


Motion
 
That the Committee recommends Council:
 
  1. That the report be received and noted.
 
  1. That the information contained in the report be considered in formulating a recommendation to Council on the Long Term Financial Plan parameters 2026/27, to guide the preparation of the draft 2026/27 budget.
 
  1. That the assumptions detailed in Appendix 1 be endorsed, specifically:
  1. that the Deloittee Access Economics forecast CPI of 3.71% is used as the basis for the LTFP 
  2. the Property Growth assumption is 1.1%that salaries budget is based on the Wages Price Index of 3.2%
  3. that the Long Term Financial Plan provide for a debt level at Year 10 of up to 20% of Year 1 rates revenue within the LTFP model. 
  4. the LTFP assumes asset values will grow with CPI, and in between full valuations Council applies an indexation to the replacement cost using the Australian Bureau of Statistics Construction Industry Price

  1. That Council consider all scenarios at the Council Workshop and meeting on Tuesday, 10th March noting that the Corporate Services Committee has a preference for scenario 3.

  2. That a further report on implementing differential rating for short term rentals be presented to the Corporate Services Committee and Council for consideration as part of the draft budget 2026/27.    

4.2 QUARTERLY BUDGET REVIEW - DECEMBER 2025


Motion 

That the Committee recommends to Council:
 
  1. That the report be received and noted.

  2. That the 2025/26 Budget be amended to recognise the additional income received to date, together with the associated expenditure as detailed in Appendix 1 to this report.

  3. That the revised Budgeted Annual Financial Statements as detailed in Appendix 2 which have been recast to include the impact of the December Q2 budget Review are adopted.
  

4.3 END OF QUARTER FINANCIAL REPORT - DECEMBER 2025


Motion 
 
 That the Committee recommends to Council:
 
1. That the report be received and noted.

4.4 QUARTERLY UPDATE TO COUNCIL'S DELEGATIONS


Motion
  
That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That the Council resolves to grant the delegation of powers and functions of the Council as provided for in the attached instrument of delegation (Appendix 1).
 
  1. In exercise of the power contained in Section 44 of the Local Government Act 1999 the powers and functions under the following Acts and specified in Appendix 2 to the report dated 2 March 2026 and titled 'Quarterly Update to Council's Delegations' (delegated to the person occupying the position of Chief Executive Officer of the Council) are hereby amended this 10 day of March 2026, by deleting the parts struck out and adding the parts underlined as set out in Appendix 2 subject to the conditions and/or limitations (if any) specified in Appendix 2.
 
Dog and Cat Management Act 1995
Local Government Act 1999
Planning, Development and Infrastructure Act 2016
 
The amendment of these delegations will come into operation on 20 March 2026.
 
  1. In exercise of the power contained in Section 100 of the Planning, Development and Infrastructure Act 2016 the powers and functions under the Planning, Development and Infrastructure Act 2016 and specified in Appendix 3 to the report dated 2 March 2026 and titled 'Quarterly Update to Council's Delegations' (delegated to the person occupying the position of Chief Executive Officer of the Council) are hereby amended this 10 day of March 2026, by deleting the parts struck out and adding the parts underlined as set out in Appendix 3 subject to the conditions and/or limitations (if any) specified in Appendix 3.
 
The amendment of these delegations will come into operation on 20 March 2026.

4.5 POLICY REVIEW - COUNCIL MEMBERS USE OF COUNCIL HARDWARE AND SOFTWARE POLICY


Motion 
 
  1. That the Committee recommends to Council that the Council Members Use of Council Hardware and Software Policy attached in Appendix 1 is endorsed and that the Policy will take effect from March 2026.

4.6 POLICY REVIEW - COUNCIL MEMBER MOBILE DEVICE POLICY (INCLUDING BYOMD)


Motion 
 
  1. That the Committee recommends to Council that the Council Member Mobile Device Policy (Including BYOMD) Policy attached in Appendix 1 is endorsed and that the Policy will take effect from March 2026.

4.7 POLICIES FOR REVIEW - MINOR CHANGES ONLY 


Motion 
 
  1. That the Committee recommends to Council that the revised policies, listed below, be adopted;
 
  • Breast Feeding Policy in Appendix 1
  • Children and Vulnerable Persons Policy in Appendix 2
  • City of Charles Sturt Business Recognition Awards Event Sponsorship Policy in Appendix 3
  • Civic Recognition and Events Policy in Appendix 4
  • Customer Experience Policy in Appendix 5
  • Dog and Cat Management Policy in Appendix 6
  • Environmental Sustainability Policy in Appendix 7
  • Expiation Notice Review Policy in Appendix 8
  • Plant, Equipment and Fleet Management Policy in Appendix 9
  • Privately Funded Code Amendments Policy in Appendix 10
  • Volunteer Policy in Appendix 11
  • Volunteer Code of Conduct Policy in Appendix 12
  

Council adopts the recommendations of the Committee as printed in the Minutes of this Committee.

Carried

b.
information the disclosure of which (i) could reasonably be expected to confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting, or proposing to conduct, business, or to prejudice the commercial position of the council; and (ii) would, on balance, be contrary to the public interest.

Questions on Notice have been received from Councillor Katriona Kinsella in relation to the Jubilee Redevelopment Master Plan Scenario 3 (revised) – Local Community Access to School Ovals and Community Engagement Approach Stage 2.


Questions
Councillor Katriona Kinsella has provided the following preamble in relation to her questions on notice:

The endorsed Motion at the 23 February 2026 Council Meeting regarding Item 6.1 Jubilee Redevelopment Master Plan will see Scenario 3 (revised) pursued by the council administration.
 
Scenario 3 (revised) infers the council administration will pursue a Shared Use Agreement between West Lakes Shores Primary School (via the Department for Education) and the City of Charles Sturt to activate the school oval for out of school hours use with the potential for lighting installation.
 
The 23 February 2026 Council Meeting noted:
 
 

It is noted that progressing a Shared Use Agreement with the identified parties is an important aspect of unlocking longer term formal and informal recreational uses in this reserve / suburb. Further, it is also an important pathway to secure appropriate access to playing fields for sporting clubs that currently utilise Jubilee Reserve that may be impacted by the progression of Scenario 3 (revised).

 


  1. What is the status of negotiations between City of Charles Sturt and West Lakes Shores Primary School / Department for Education in regards to a Joint Use Agreement? What is the current timeline for an executed agreement? What is the likely term (i.e. years) of that agreement?

  2. How is endorsement of Scenario 3 (revised) related to the endorsed Motion at the 17 November 2025 Strategic and Engagement Committee Meeting regarding Item 4.3 – Local Community Access to School Ovals?

  3. Presuming negotiations proceed and will lead to the intended outcomes of a Joint Use Agreement between the identified parties, what priority will be given to sporting clubs currently engaged at Jubilee Reserve that may be impacted by the Council’s endorsement of Scenario 3 (revised)?

  4. Can the report to Council on the next stages of the Jubilee Redevelopment Masterplan include reference to any financial impacts sporting clubs currently engaged in activities at Jubilee Reserve are likely to experience as a result of pursuing Scenario 3 (revised)?

  5. Will appropriate orientation of soccer pitches at Jubilee Reserve be considered as part of the Community Engagement Approach Stage 2?

  6. Should an executed Shared Use Agreement between the identified parties be achieved, how will this impact the key steps and timelines of the endorsed Community Engagement Approach Stage 2?



Questions and Answers
  1. What is the status of negotiations between City of Charles Sturt and West Lakes Shores Primary School / Department for Education in regards to a Joint Use Agreement? What is the current timeline for an executed agreement? What is the likely term (i.e. years) of that agreement?
The Strategic and Engagement Committee (SE 17/11/25, Item 4.3) recommended that Council delegate authority to the CEO to negotiate and finalise Joint Use Agreements with the Department for Education and the governing bodies of Woodville High School and West Lakes Shore Primary School.

Since Council’s meeting on 23 February 2025, negotiations have progressed in accordance with this delegation. Council staff have met with the Department for Education’s Strategic Policy and External Partnerships division, along with the West Lakes Shore Primary School Principal and Governing Council Chair, to formalise structured shared-use arrangements, including: access, lighting infrastructure, maintenance responsibilities, cost-sharing and community benefit. A subsequent meeting has also been held with the Department for Education’s Capital Projects and Technical Services division, which typically assist in preparing the requisite documentation.

As the agreement will be prepared by the State Government’s Crown Solicitor’s Office, it is not possible to confirm an actual execution date. However, there is strong intent and goodwill from all parties to progress the agreement promptly. 

A further update will be provided to Council when Jubilee Reserve Stage 2 Community Engagement results are presented.

Joint Use Agreements of this nature are typically medium- to long-term arrangements (generally 10+ years) to align with the life of lighting and infrastructure investments.

  1. How is endorsement of Scenario 3 (revised) related to the endorsed Motion at the 17 November 2025 Strategic and Engagement Committee Meeting regarding Item 4.3 – Local Community Access to School Ovals?
The 17 November 2025 report (SE 17/11/25, Item 4.3) established the Local Community Access to School Ovals Program as a strategic framework to relieve pressure on Council-managed ovals through structured school partnerships and coordinated shared-use planning and provide access to additional areas of open space for community use.

Scenario 3 (revised) for Jubilee Reserve aligns with this approach, as it supports unlocking additional open space capacity through a structured Joint Use Agreement and targeted infrastructure improvements to underutilised school grounds. This will provide increased capacity for growing clubs and associations, maintain continuity of access to playing fields, and enhance the overall utilisation of existing community assets.

Accordingly, endorsement of Scenario 3 (revised) and the Local Community Access to School Ovals framework are strategically interconnected.

  1. Presuming negotiations proceed and will lead to the intended outcomes of a Joint Use Agreement between the identified parties, what priority will be given to sporting clubs currently engaged at Jubilee Reserve that may be impacted by the Council’s endorsement of Scenario 3 (revised)?
Yes. It is recommended that priority access to the unlocked school facilities would be provided to sporting clubs/associations currently based at Jubilee Reserve that may be impacted by Council’s endorsement of Scenario 3 (revised), including the North West Junior Soccer Association and SMOSH West Lakes Junior Football Club.

Any additional users would be considered jointly by the school and Council, with careful regard to maintaining the quality and condition of the playing surface. This approach ensures school use remains protected while supporting sustainable community access and long-term asset performance.

  1. Can the report to Council on the next stages of the Jubilee Redevelopment Masterplan include reference to any financial impacts sporting clubs currently engaged in activities at Jubilee Reserve are likely to experience as a result of pursuing Scenario 3 (revised)?
Yes. The next report will include an assessment of financial impacts on stakeholders in continuing their normal sporting activities within the Jubilee Reserve precinct during the construction phase associated with Scenario 3 (revised). 

This will consider each stakeholder currently operating at Jubilee Reserve and outline proposed mitigation measures to manage transitional impacts. While some temporary disruption or additional costs can occur during sporting facility upgrades, works will be carefully planned and managed to minimise impacts, with appropriate support measures implemented to assist stakeholders wherever reasonably practicable.

 

  1. Will appropriate orientation of soccer pitches at Jubilee Reserve be considered as part of the Community Engagement Approach Stage 2?
Yes. Appropriate orientation of soccer pitches at Jubilee Reserve will be considered as part of the Stage 2 Community Engagement process, with particular regard to player and spectator safety and best-practice design standards. This will be undertaken collaboratively with the project architects, relevant stakeholders and Council officers.

  1. Should an executed Shared Use Agreement between the identified parties be achieved, how will this impact the key steps and timelines of the endorsed Community Engagement Approach Stage 2?
Work is actively progressing to finalise a Shared Use Agreement between Council and the Department for Education, with negotiations advancing in a coordinated and deliberate manner. 

The Stage 2 Community Engagement Approach will continue in accordance with the endorsed CEA steps and timelines. While the Shared Use Agreement is an enabling component of the broader project, it is being progressed in parallel to ensure alignment without interrupting the engagement program. This approach maintains project momentum, ensuring that Stage 2 consultation proceeds as endorsed while the agreement is being finalised.

We acknowledge the contributions and important role that Aboriginal people continue to play within our local community in Charles Sturt. Almighty Father from Whom all goodness flows, grant unto us qualities of wisdom justice and tolerance, that we the civic leaders of this community may govern in harmony and concord.

We also remember and give thanks for those, our sons and daughters, who gave their lives for Australia.

The Operations Committee was held on Monday, 16 March 2026.


Moved: Councillor Edgar Agius
Seconded: Councillor Quin Tran

That having considered the recommendations of the Committee which has read and considered the reports in the agenda related to items:

 

4.1 PRESENTATION - TRIMMER PARADE STORMWATER DRAINAGE PROJECT


Motion
 
That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That the progress of the Trimmer Parade Stormwater Drainage project be noted. 
 
  1. That staff be thanked for the presentation and the presentation be included in the minutes.

4.2 REVISED MEMORIALS POLICY - MEMORIAL PLAQUES ON STATE-OWNED JETTIES


Note the motion to this item lapsed for want of a seconder.

4.3 CITY OPERATIONS CAPITAL WORKS & OPERATING PROGRAM VARIATIONS


Motion
 
That the Committee recommends to the Council: 
 
  1. That the following variations to the Capital Works Program or Annual Operating Program be approved and adjusted in the financial statements at the next quarterly review as they involve transfers between renewal and new/upgrade works and or new projects to be funded by unbudgeted income:
 
  1. Budgeted expenditure for Percy Fox Grandstand Changeroom (Project 3549 - Upgrade) be increased by $170,000 from reallocated funds in the 2025/26 Council Building Renewals (Project 3824 - Renewal).
 
  1. Budgeted expenditure for Waterproofing the West - Freshwater Lake Integration (Project 3490 - Renewal) be increased by $345,000 from savings in the Living Streets Road Reconstruction and Streetscape Program (Project 3542 - Upgrade).
 
  1. That by endorsing the variations listed in 1. above, Council is endorsing a variation to the approved Asset Management Plan renewal schedule where relevant.

4.4 ELECTRIC VEHICLE CHARGING STATIONS UPDATE 


Motion
 
That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That Council notes the JOLT Charge Pty Ltd (JOLT) contract amendments to:
 
  1. remove the minimum number of electric vehicle chargers that JOLT is required to install under their contract, and 
 
  1. remove the exclusivity clause within the contract, to enable other operators to install electric vehicle chargers on public land within the City of Charles Sturt.
 
  1. That Council notes that staff will explore opportunities for further electric vehicle charging infrastructure and approach the market where appropriate locations are identified.


Council adopts the recommendations of the Committee as printed in the Minutes of this Committee.

Carried Unanimously

The City of Charles Sturt has a duty to administer the Dog and Cat Management Act 1995 (the Act), and related Dog and Cat Management Regulations (2017) relating to dogs and cats within our City. The State Government are seeking feedback on the proposed new Dog and Cat Management (Breeder Reforms) Regulations 2025 (the Regulations) and associated Standards and Guidelines for Breeding Dogs and Cats 2026.  

This report highlights general support for the proposed amendments to the Regulations and Standards and Guidelines. It also provides additional feedback regarding previously endorsed Council positions relating to animal management, including the need for a consistent, statewide approach to cat management, additional detention facilities for dogs and cats, and the fair retention for registration fees remitted to the Board (the Dog and Cat Management Fund). This report provides a detailed submission in response to the requested feedback, including additional opportunities being raised, so that the objects of the Act may be better achieved. 



Moved: Councillor Kelly Thomas
Seconded: Councillor Nicholas Le Lacheur

Motion

  1. That the feedback to the proposed amendments to the Dog and Cat Management Regulations (2025) and Standards and Guidelines for Breeding Dogs and Cats 2026 and requested by the Dog and Cat Management Board, as presented in Appendix 5, be endorsed by Council for submission to the State Government.
     
Carried Unanimously

A Motion on Notice has been received from Councillor Nicole Mazeika in relation to rescinding a resolution of Council from 23 February 2026 relating to Item 2.2.2 - 4.1 (CL 23/02/26, Item 2.2.2 - 4.1), regarding the tree located adjacent 38 Flinders Parade, Flinders Park.



Moved: Councillor Nicole MazeikaSeconded: Councillor Stuart Ghent

Motion
  1. That the following resolution passed by at the Ordinary meeting of Council on 23 February 2026 in relation to the Operations Committee Item 4.1 – Tree Located Adjacent 38 Flinders Parade, Flinders Park:

1. That the tree located on the verge adjacent 38 Flinders Parade, Flinders Park, assessed against Council’s Tree and Vegetation Policy as suitable for retention, be considered for removal noting that any removal would also require an approved Development Application due to it being classified as a significant tree.

2. That community consultation regarding the removal of the tree located on the verge adjacent 38 Flinders Parade, Flinders Park be undertaken.

3. That the results of the community consultation be referred to the Operations Committee for consideration and to make a final recommendation to Council.

Be rescinded, and

2. That Councillor Mazeika's notes are included in the Minutes.
Carried
Division called by Councillor Nicole Mazeika

Voters
For:Councillor - Alice Campbell, Councillor - Stuart Ghent, Councillor - Katriona Kinsella, Councillor - Nicholas Le Lacheur, Councillor - Nicole Mazeika, Councillor - Peter Ppiros, Councillor - Kelly Thomas, Councillor - Quin Tran, Councillor - Rachele Tullio, Councillor - George Turelli (10)
Against:Councillor - Edgar Agius, Councillor - Tom Scheffler (2)
Not Vote:Mayor Angela Evans (1)
The Motion to Item 7.1. was Carried


Councillor Mazeika Notes:

I rise to move that we rescind the previous resolution regarding the tree at 38 Flinders Parade, Flinders Park.
Before anything else, it’s important we ground this discussion in fact.
The tree in question is a mature Wandoo, estimated to be between 80 and 120 years old. Over the past two decades, it has been assessed 14 separate times, by both Council and independent arborists and every single assessment has reached the same conclusion: this tree should be retained.
Similarly, council has no record of any injury caused directly by the tree.
 
The most recent independent report confirms it is in good health, structurally sound, and presents a low level of risk. There are no arboriculture grounds to justify its removal.
So what we are dealing with here is not a dangerous tree. It is not a dying tree.
It is a healthy, significant tree, one that contributes meaningfully to our landscape, biodiversity and neighbourhood character.
 
Which brings us to the real issue. This is about whether we, as a Council, stand by our own commitment to protecting our urban canopy, or whether that commitment only applies when it is convenient to its location.
We have heard concerns around accessibility, sightlines and verge condition. These are valid concerns, and they absolutely deserve to be addressed. But they do not justify the removal of a healthy, significant tree.
 
Because when the issue is infrastructure conflict, the first question should always be:
what can we change around the tree before we remove the tree itself? in this case, that question has not been fully explored.
Modern streetscape design across Australia is very clear on this point; mature trees are treated as essential infrastructure.  This is what all our significant trees should be viewed as; ESSENTIAL INFRASTRUCTURE. Footpaths should be realigned, parking should be adjusted, and innovative materials need to be used to work around root zones.
Because the principle is simple:
infrastructure can be redesigned, mature trees cannot be replaced.
 
If we remove this tree, we are not just losing something aesthetic.
We are losing decades of environmental benefit of shade, urban cooling, habitat—and we are losing it permanently.
And we would also be asking our community to fund that loss. The removal of a tree of this size, along with associated works, would cost tens of thousands of dollars of ratepayers’ money—money that could instead be invested into improving the verge, addressing accessibility, and delivering a solution that benefits everyone.
 
We also need to acknowledge context.
The concern raised comes from a property owner who purchased the home approximately five years ago—at a time when this tree was already well established and part of the streetscape.
This was a conscious decision to buy into a street defined, in part, by its mature canopy.
That context matters when we consider fairness, precedent, and the expectations we set as a Council.
And we must also consider precedent more broadly.
If we allow the removal of a healthy, significant tree primarily due to inconvenience, then we send a very clear message to our community, that canopy protection is conditional.
That is not protection.
 
Street by street, decision by decision, we risk eroding the very canopy we say we value, leaving future generations with hotter, harsher and less liveable neighbourhoods.
 
Rescinding this motion is not about dismissing community concerns. It is about respecting them enough to find a better, more reasonable solutions.
 
And that is exactly what this motion delivers.
The alternative before us is reasonable, practical and balanced:
improve and potentially realign the footpath to maintain accessibility,
consider a no-parking zone to improve safety,
and recognise the tree’s significance through education and thoughtful design. To look at innovation and shared use spaces.
 
Ultimately, this decision comes down to a simple question:
Do we remove a healthy 100-year-old tree? or do we design more thoughtfully around it to preserve it well into our grandchildren’s future?
Tonight, we have the opportunity to pause, to reconsider, and to demonstrate that our commitment to our urban Tree canopy and is real.
I ask you to support this rescission motion—to ensure we deliver a reasonable,  though-out and responsible outcome for our community now and more importantly into the future.

Thank you.


Moved: Councillor Nicole MazeikaSeconded: Councillor Stuart Ghent

Motion

  1. That the tree located adjacent to 38 Flinders Parade, Flinders Park and assessed against Council’s Tree & Vegetation Policy as suitable for retention be retained, and that Council investigate opportunities to improve the surrounding area, including: 

  • improving the footpath to improve accessibility and investigate any innovative designs or products that could be used around the tree;
  • create a no-parking zone around the tree to improve safety and access; and
  • installing an educational element (such as signage or a small plaque) to inform the community about the tree’s age, species, and its significance.
  • Report on what other local metro council are doing with trees of significance to keep them within the communities.


Carried Unanimously

The City of Charles Sturt acknowledges and pays respect to the traditional custodians of the land, the Kaurna people of the Adelaide plains. We pay our respect to Elders past, present and emerging. We respect their spiritual beliefs and connections to land which are of continuing importance to the Kaurna people of today. We acknowledge the contributions and important role that Aboriginal people continue to play within our local community in Charles Sturt. We also respect the culture of Aboriginal people visiting from other areas of South Australia and Australia.

Almighty Father from Whom all goodness flows, grant unto us qualities of wisdom justice and tolerance, that we the civic leaders of this community may govern in harmony and concord.

This we ask in Thy name. 

We also remember and give thanks for those, our sons and daughters, who gave their lives for Australia. 

Lest we forget.

The Corporate Services Committee was held on Tuesday, 7 April 2026.


Moved: Councillor Michael McEwen
Seconded: Councillor Alice Campbell

That having considered the recommendations of the Committee which has read and considered the reports in the agenda related to all items, with the exception of Items 4.1 and 4.2:


4.3 POLICIES FOR REVIEW - MINOR CHANGES ONLY 

Motion 
 
  1. That the Committee recommends to Council that the revised policies, listed below, be adopted;
 
  • Sporting and Community Clubs Loan Guarantees Policy in Appendix 1

 

Council adopts the recommendations of the Committee as printed in the Minutes of this Committee.

Carried Unanimously


Moved: Councillor Michael McEwen
Seconded: Councillor Alice Campbell

4.1 REVIEW OF CAPITAL AND ANNUAL OPERATING PROJECT BUDGET BIDS 2026/27 FOR INCLUSION IN DRAFT ANNUAL BUSINESS PLAN FOR COMMUNITY CONSULTATION


Motion
 
That the Committee recommends to Council:
 
  1. That the Annual Operating Budget Bids as attached as Appendix 2 be included in the Draft Annual Business Plan 2026/27 for community consultation, with the following updates (include budget bids to be deleted, added or amended). 
 
  • Project PBB-0002686, Jetty Memorial Plaques, $15,000, be deleted due to a duplicate project (Project PBB-0002691, Memorial Infrastructure at Henley and Grange Jetties).
  
  1. That the Capital Renewal Budget Bids as attached as Appendix 3 be included in the Draft Annual Business Plan 2026/27 for community consultation.
 
  1. That the Capital New and Upgrade Budget Bids as attached in Appendix 4 be included in the Draft Annual Business Plan 2026/27 for community consultation, with the following updates (include budget bids to be deleted, added or amended).
  
  • PBB-0002686, Memorial Infrastructure at Henley and Grange Jetties, be changed to include $15,000 income.
  • PBB-00002671, Euston Terrace Greening, $15,000, be deleted.
  • PBB-00002655, Euston Terrace and Malcolm Street, West Croydon - Intersection Artwork and Tree Planting, $35,000, be increased by $15,000 to a total budget bid of $50,000 and include the project scope from budget bid PBB-00002671, and Euston Terrace Greening and consultation and tree planting in Phillip Street.
  • PBB-00002669, Rowley Park, Brompton - Additional play equipment and landscaping, $60,000, be updated to include Cr Alice as the requesting councillor.
  • PBB-00002673, that the bid title be amended to: Carnegie Reserve Sporting Precinct - Design and Consultation for New Public Toilet and Dog Park, and that Cr Kelly be added as the requesting Elected Member along with Cr Nicole.
  • PBB-00002653, Bus Shelter Installation-Stop 27-Port Road-Cheltenham - that Council will seek a status update from the State Government regarding potential funding.
Carried 

Councillor - Nicole Mazeika left the meeting at 7:50 PM.

Moved: Councillor George Turelli
Seconded: Councillor Michael McEwen

4.2 DIFFERENTIAL RATING ON SHORT STAY ACCOMMODATION


Motion 
 
That the Committee recommends to Council that:
 
  1. The report be received and noted.

  2. That Short Term rental accommodation be defined as an entire dwelling (i.e. not individual rooms or partial dwellings) being available for 183 days (6 months) of the financial year.

  3. That the differential rating of short term rentals be investigated and be considered as part of the 2027/28 annual budget process.

  4. That the next report includes a cost benefit analysis focusing on additional resources and implementation costs required to implement a profitable and sustainable revenue base.
Carried Unanimously

This report provides an overview of the successful Age Friendly SA Grant Application provided to conduct comprehensive community-led consultation and develop an action plan to compliment the new Ageing Well model for the City of Charles Sturt. 

The report outlines what the grant will enable Council to deliver, including the scope, approach and proposed outcomes of the project. The initiative will support the development of the City of Charles Sturt’s first Ageing Well Plan through community-led consultation, alongside a pilot suite of wellbeing programs informed by those insights.

Community-led consultation is the primary purpose of this project, ensuring an Ageing Well Plan is grounded in lived experience and informs future investment where Council will continue to have the greatest impact. 

The initiative aligns with Council’s Community Vision 2040, Ageing in Charles Sturt Policy, Community Development objectives, and the South Australian Government’s Plan for Ageing Well 2026–2036.

General Declaration of Interest
Councillor - Katriona Kinsella declared a general conflict of interest pursuant to Section 75B of the Local Government Act for Item 6.4. The nature of Councillor - Katriona Kinsella's general conflict is that while she has no direct role related to the program in question, the department providing the funding is her employer. Councillor - Katriona Kinsella dealt with the conflict of interest in the following transparent and accountable way and remaining in the room, sitting with staff for the duration of Item 6.4 and not participating in the debate or vote.


Moved: Councillor Nicole MazeikaSeconded: Councillor George Turelli

Motion

  1. That Council acknowledges and accepts the Office for Ageing Well grant offer of $50,000 through the 2025–2026 Age Friendly SA Grants Program.

  2. That Council notes securing this grant provides additional capacity to undertake comprehensive community‑led consultation and connection opportunities with community of the endorsed Ageing Well Model, and is in addition to (and separate from) the operational implementation proposed through the 2026/27 budget bid.

  3. That Council notes this funding will help inform the continued development and implementation of the City of Charles Sturt’s new Ageing Well Program and Ageing Well Plan.

  4. That a further report, including evaluation outcomes and recommendations for future initiatives and action plan, be presented to Council upon project completion.

Carried Unanimously

This report provides for the appointment of people to the Building Fire Safety Committee and adjustments to the terms of reference for the committee under the Planning, Development and Infrastructure Act 2016.  



Moved: Councillor George Turelli
Seconded: Councillor Katriona Kinsella

Motion

  1. That Council adopts the City of Charles Sturt Council Building Fire Safety Committee Establishment and Administrative Procedure contained in Appendix 1. 

  1. That the following people are appointed to the Building Fire Safety Committee:

    a. The following staff being a person appointed by the Council and who holds prescribed qualifications in building surveying pursuant to Section 157(17)(a)(i);
          Marija Vjestica
          Byron Edwards
          Danny Hardi
          Tony Travaglione
          Elio Calo
          Paul Skoumbros.
     
    NOTE: Only one staff member from the list shall participate on the Committee at a scheduled meeting.

    b. A Person approved by the Chief Officer of the South Australian Metropolitan Fire Service (MFS) as being an authorised MFS officer under Part 3 Division 5 of the Fire and Emergency Services Act 2005 pursuant to Section 157(17)(a)(ii).
     
    NOTE: Only one person approved by the Chief Officer of the SAMFS shall participate on the Committee at a scheduled meeting.

    c. Marija Vjestica or Byron Edwards are appointed by the Council as person(s) with expertise in the area of fire safety pursuant to Section 157(17)(a)(iii). 
    NOTE: Only one of either Marija Vjestica or Byron Edwards shall participate on any scheduled committee meeting.

  2. The Council appoints Byron Edwards as the Presiding Member of the BFSC.  The Council appoints Marija Vjestica as Deputy Presiding Member of the BFSC.

The City of Charles Sturt acknowledges and pays respect to the traditional custodians of the land, the Kaurna people of the Adelaide plains. We pay our respect to Elders past, present and emerging. We respect their spiritual beliefs and connections to land which are of continuing importance to the Kaurna people of today. We acknowledge the contributions and important role that Aboriginal people continue to play within our local community in Charles Sturt. We also respect the culture of Aboriginal people visiting from other areas of South Australia and Australia.

Almighty Father from Whom all goodness flows, grant unto us qualities of wisdom justice and tolerance, that we the civic leaders of this community may govern in harmony and concord.

This we ask in Thy name. 

We also remember and give thanks for those, our sons and daughters, who gave their lives for Australia. 

Lest we forget.

The Strategic and Engagement Committee was held on Monday, 20 April 2026.


Moved: Councillor Nicole MazeikaSeconded: Councillor Peter Ppiros

That having considered the recommendations of the Committee which has read and considered the reports in the agenda related to all items, with the exception of Item 4.5:

 

4.1. - PRESENTATION - YOUR NEIGHBOURHOOD PLAN (YNP) AND LOCAL CENTRES REVITALISATION FLAGSHIP INITIATIVES UPDATE

 

Motion

 

  1. That the presentation be received and noted.

 

  1. That staff be thanked for their presentation and a copy of the presentation be included in the Minutes.

 

4.2. - BULAHDELAH RESERVE BIODIVERSITY RESERVE - OUTCOMES OF COMMUNITY CONSULTATION

 

Motion 

 

  1. That Council notes the outcomes of community consultation for the Biodiversity Reserve at Bulahdelah Reserve, as outlined in Appendix 1 and Appendix 2.

 

  1. That Council endorses progression of the project to concept design development for Bulahdelah Reserve as a biodiversity-focused reserve, consistent with community feedback.

 

  1. That Council notes a further round of targeted community engagement will be undertaken in accordance with the Community Engagement Approach outlined in Appendix 3.

 

4.3. - PROPOSAL TO AMEND MIRANI COURT RESERVE COMMUNITY LAND MANAGEMENT PLAN

 

Motion 

 

  1. That Council notes the request and petition provided by the registered proprietor of 1A Mirani Court, West Lakes Shore (Mirani's Cafe) (Appendix 1).

 

  1. That Council endorse the draft amended Community Land Management Plan - Mirani Court Reserve (Appendix 2) and Community Engagement Approach (Appendix 3) for public consultation.

 

  1. That Council resolves to undertake community consultation to amend the Mirani Court Reserve Community Land Management Plan in accordance with section 197 of the Local Government Act 1999 and Council's Public Consultation Policy.

 

  1. That a further report be brought to Council containing the outcome of the public consultation process.

 

4.4. - COUNCIL ASSESSMENT PANEL SEPTEMBER AND DECEMBER 2025 QUARTERLY REPORTS

 

Motion 

  1. That the Committee recommends to Council that the report be received and noted.

 

4.6. - PROPOSED DOG REGISTRATION FEES 2026/2027

 

Motion 

 

  1. That Council endorses the proposed dog registration fee structure for 2026/2027 as detailed in Appendix 1.

  

Council adopts the recommendations of the Committee as printed in the Minutes of this Committee.

Carried Unanimously


General Declaration of Interest

Mayor Angela Evans declared a general conflict of interest pursuant to Section 75B of the Local Government Act for Item 2.2.1 - 4.5. The nature of Mayor Angela Evans' general conflict is her role as a Board member of Green Adelaide. Mayor Angela Evans dealt with the conflict of interest in the following transparent and accountable way by remaining in the room, sitting with staff for the duration of Item 2.2.1 - 4.5 and not participating in the debate or vote.

In the absence of the Mayor and Deputy Mayor, Councillor Agius took the Chair at 7:07 PM.

Moved: Councillor Nicole MazeikaSeconded: Councillor Quin Tran

4.5. - GREEN ADELAIDE COOLER, GREENER, WILDER PROGRAM - ACCEPTANCE OF GRANT FUNDING

This report seeks Council approval to accept an offer from the Department for Environment and Water (DEW) to purchase unallocated groundwater access entitlements in the Adelaide Plains Prescribed Wells Area for public benefit purposes. The purchase will support irrigation of public open spaces and form part of Council’s long-term water security strategy, utilising groundwater resources in the southern areas of the City where extension of the piped recycled water network is not economically feasible.




Moved: Councillor Alice Campbell
Seconded: Councillor Stuart Ghent

Motion

  1. That Council accepts the offer from the Department for Environment and Water (DEW) to purchase 500,000 kL of unallocated groundwater access entitlements in the Adelaide Plains Prescribed Wells Area for public benefit purposes, in accordance with the Instrument of Agreement - WLA-757931 (Appendix 1).

  2. That Council authorises the Chief Executive Officer to execute the Instrument of Agreement and any associated documentation required to finalise the purchase of groundwater access entitlements.

  3. That Council notes the strategic approach to water supply to minimise the use of potable (mains) water for irrigation of reserves and sportsgrounds. This is to be achieved through maintaining and expanding the existing recycled stormwater network in the northern areas, and utilising groundwater (bore water) in the southern areas where it represents the most practical and cost-effective solution. The additional 500,000 kL of groundwater access will increase capacity to support this strategy in the southern areas.

  4. That Council notes that the procurement of ground water is in alignment with the existing Water Infrastructure Asset Management Plan 2024-2034 and requires no change to LTFP or existing capital budgets.

Carried Unanimously

  2. In accordance with Section 90(3)(d)(i) and (ii) of the Local Government Act 1999, Council is satisfied that it is necessary that the public be excluded to consider the information contained in the report ITEM 11.1 - MAJOR EVENT CONSIDERATION on the following grounds:
d.

The City of Charles Sturt acknowledges and pays respect to the traditional custodians of the land, the Kaurna people of the Adelaide plains. We pay our respect to Elders past, present and emerging. We respect their spiritual beliefs and connections to land which are of continuing importance to the Kaurna people of today. We acknowledge the contributions and important role that Aboriginal people continue to play within our local community in Charles Sturt. We also respect the culture of Aboriginal people visiting from other areas of South Australia and Australia.

Almighty Father from Whom all goodness flows, grant unto us qualities of wisdom justice and tolerance, that we the civic leaders of this community may govern in harmony and concord.

This we ask in Thy name. 

We also remember and give thanks for those, our sons and daughters, who gave their lives for Australia. 

Lest we forget.

The Corporate Services Committee was held on Monday, 4 May 2026.


Moved: Councillor Alice Campbell
Seconded: Councillor Peter Ppiros

That having considered the recommendations of the Committee which has read and considered the reports in the agenda related to items:


4.1. - SAVINGS AND PRODUCTIVITY FRAMEWORK PRESENTATION AND REPORT
 
Motion 
 
That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That the Committee receives and notes the Savings and Productivity Framework, as contained in Appendix 1.
 
4.2. - MARCH 2026 QUARTERLY BUDGET REVIEW 
 
Motion 
 
That the Committee recommends to Council:
 
  1. That the report be received and noted.
 
  1. That the 2025/26 Budget be amended to recognise revisions to income received and expenditures to date, as detailed in Appendix 1 to this report.
 
  1. That the revised Budgeted Annual Financial Statements as detailed in Appendix 2 which have been recast to include the impact of the March Q3 budget Review are adopted.
 
4.3. - MARCH 2026 END OF QUARTER FINANCIAL REPORT
 
Motion 
 
That the Committee recommends to Council:
 
  1. That the report be received and noted.
 
4.4. - 2025/26 RATE REBATE REPORT
 
Motion 
 
 That the Committee recommends to Council:
 
  1. That the report be received and noted.
 
4.5. - QUARTERLY UPDATE TO COUNCIL'S DELEGATIONS
 
Motion
 
That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That the Council resolves to grant the delegation of powers and functions of the Council as provided for in the attached instrument of delegation (Appendix 1).

  2. In exercise of the power contained in Section 44 of the Local Government Act 1999 the powers and functions under the following Acts and specified in Appendix 2 to the report dated 4 May 2026 and titled 'Quarterly Update to Council's Delegations' (delegated to the person occupying the position of Chief Executive Officer of the Council) are hereby amended on 11 May 2026, by deleting the parts struck out and adding the parts underlined as set out in Appendix 2 subject to the conditions and/or limitations (if any) specified in Appendix 2.
 
Dog and Cat Management Act 1995
Local Government Act 1999
Local Government (Elections) Act 1999
Planning, Development and Infrastructure Act 2016

 The amendment of these delegations will come into operation on 22 May 2026.
 
4.6. - POLICY REVIEW - PLAY SPACE POLICY
 
Motion 

That the Committee recommends to Council that:
 
  1. That the Committee recommends to Council that the Policy attached in Appendix 1 is endorsed and that the Policy will take effect from May 2026.
 
  1. Additional dot point be included under section 3.
 
  • Play space provision and design will also be guided by the amount of open space available in a suburb and local area.
 
4.7. - POLICIES FOR REVIEW - MINOR CHANGES ONLY
 
Motion 
 
That the Committee recommends to Council that:
 
  1. The revised policies, listed below, be adopted;
  • Contaminated Site Policy in Appendix 1
  • Enforcement Policy in Appendix 2
  • External Grants Funding Policy in Appendix 3
  • Fraud and Corruption Management Policy in Appendix 4
  • Internal Review of Council Decision Policy in Appendix 5

 

Council adopts the recommendations of the Committee as printed in the Minutes of this Committee.

Carried Unanimously

This report is provided for information to support Elected Members’ understanding of the cultural, historical and environmental significance of the Grange Lakes area within the Kaurna landscape of Witongga. It outlines how First Nations engagement associated with the draft budget Annual Operating budget bid PBB-00002611 Karrawirra Pari / Grange Creek – Cultural Interpretation, will be delivered through secured external funding under the AWSEM (Alternative Water Supply Efficiency Measures) program, following Council’s endorsement of the AWSEM grant through the report ‘Grant Acceptance from the State Government for Water Efficiency (2025-1891)’ (refer CL 27/10/25, item 2.2.3/4.1), enabling the project to proceed without reliance on Council’s proposed budget while maintaining the intended scope and outcomes. The report presents a balanced view of place by recognising both Kaurna cultural knowledge and documented colonial historical records and demonstrates how culturally informed environmental initiatives can be progressed within existing Council programs and partnerships.



Moved: Councillor Rachele Tullio
Seconded: Councillor Kelly Thomas

Motion

  1. That Council acknowledges the Grange Lakes area presents two distinct but complementary perspectives, Kaurna Cultural knowledge and Colonial Historical Records and that these perspectives each contribute to an understanding of place through a different lens.

  2. That Council acknowledges that the Grange Lakes area is situated within the traditional Kaurna landscape of Witongga (the Reedbeds), as identified through Council’s commissioned cultural mapping work detailed in Appendix 1.

  3. That Council notes that AOP budget bid PBB-00002611 Karrawirra Pari / Grange Creek – Cultural Interpretation, will be fully funded from the AWSEM Indigenous Participation Program, and notes the $65,000 will be removed from the budget.

Carried Unanimously

The Local Government Act 1999 requires that a Regional Subsidiary of Councils must have an Audit and Risk Committee. In line with the Act and Central Adelaide Waste and Recycling Authority's Charter and Committee Terms of Reference, Council's must jointly appoint a Chair to the Committee, and each Council must appoint one Member. This report seeks Council's endorsement of the CAWRA Audit and Risk Committee appointments, and recommendation that Council delegates this function to CAWRA's Board for future recruitment and appointment/s as required from time to time.

General Declaration of Interest

Councillor - Rachele Tullio Tullio declared a general conflict of interest pursuant to Section 75B of the Local Government Act for Item 6.2. The nature of Councillor - Rachele Tullio Tullio's general conflict is that she personally knows Mr Peter Brass. Councillor - Rachele Tullio Tullio dealt with the conflict of interest in the following transparent and accountable way and remaining in the room, sitting with staff for the duration of Item 6.2 and not participating in the debate or vote.


Moved: Councillor Stuart Ghent
Seconded: Councillor Kelly Thomas

Motion

  1. That Council endorse the appointment of Mr Peter Brass to the position of Independent Chair of the Central Adelaide Waste and Recycling Authority Audit and Risk Committee, noting that the appointment must be made jointly with the City of Port Adelaide Enfield.

  2. That Council endorse the appointment of Ms Pamela Lee to the position of CCS Independent Member of the Central Adelaide Waste and Recycling Authority Audit and Risk Committee.

  3. That both appointments be for an initial term of two years commencing from the date of acceptance.

  4. In exercise of the power contained in section 44 of the Local Government Act 1999 the powers and functions under the following Acts and specified below are hereby delegated this 11 day of May 2026, to the Central Adelaide Waste and Recycling Authority (CAWRA) Board subject to the conditions and/or limitations, if any, specified herein.

Local Government Act 1999
The power pursuant to Clause 30(3), Schedule 2 of the Local Government Act 1999 to determine or approve (in conjunction with the other constituent councils) the members of the subsidiary's audit committee.

Conditions/Limitations
The delegation to the CAWRA Board under Clause 30(3), Schedule 2 of the Local Government Act 1999 is limited to the determination or approval of members of the CAWRA Audit and Risk Committee.

Carried Unanimously

Questions on Notice have been received from Councillor Alice Campbell in relation to illegal dumping.

Questions
1. Can Council please provide data on the number of fines issued for illegal dumping across the whole Council area for the past two years, including total amount paid?

2. Further to this, can the Council advise on the success rate of any investigations it has taken on illegal dumping in the past two years, including identifying the offenders and retrieving fines?


Questions and Answers
1. Can Council please provide data on the number of fines issued for illegal dumping across the whole Council area for the past two years, including total amount paid?
In the past two years, there has been 254 occurrences of the rubbish being reclaimed (taken back) and Council officers have issued 36 infringement notices for littering under the Local Nuisance and Litter Control Act. Of those 36 infringement notices: 8 were waived; 16 paid; 10 have been referred to the Fines Enforcement and Recovery Unit (FERU); and 2 are in progress. The infringement amount varies depending on the categorisation of the offence as is either $210 or $1,000 and the total amounts paid or payable for the two-year period is $20,890.

2. Further to this, can the Council advise on the success rate of any investigations it has taken on illegal dumping in the past two years, including identifying the offenders and retrieving fines?
In the past two years, Council has received 8,179 "Waste and Recycling - Dumped Rubbish" cases. This includes a range of illegal dumping from loose litter to large piles of significant items. On each occasion, an assessment is made as to whether the occurrence warrants any further investigation. Assessments for investigations and enforcement are made by Council staff in accordance with Council's Enforcement Policy. 

If the success rate is measured by rubbish that is reclaimed or taken back, this would be approximately 3% of total cases in the last two years. However, this does not necessarily indicate that the offender was able to be identified or if an infringement was issued, only that the rubbish was not removed by Council.

The City of Charles Sturt acknowledges and pays respect to the traditional custodians of the land, the Kaurna people of the Adelaide plains. We pay our respect to Elders past, present and emerging. We respect their spiritual beliefs and connections to land which are of continuing importance to the Kaurna people of today. We acknowledge the contributions and important role that Aboriginal people continue to play within our local community in Charles Sturt. We also respect the culture of Aboriginal people visiting from other areas of South Australia and Australia.

Almighty Father from Whom all goodness flows, grant unto us qualities of wisdom justice and tolerance, that we the civic leaders of this community may govern in harmony and concord.

This we ask in Thy name. 

We also remember and give thanks for those, our sons and daughters, who gave their lives for Australia. 

Lest we forget.

The Strategic and Engagement Committee was held on Monday, 18 May 2026.


Moved: Councillor Nicole Mazeika
Seconded: Councillor Peter Ppiros

That having considered the recommendations of the Committee which has read and considered the reports in the agenda related to all items, with the exception of Item 4.4:

 

4.1. - PRESENTATION - LIBRARIES FUNDING - SUPPORT LGA SOUTH AUSTRALIA ADVOCACY 
 
Motion
 
That Council: 
 
  1. Notes that the absence of annual CPI indexation in the current State–Local Government public libraries funding agreement continues to erode the real value of State funding over time.
 
  1. Recognises as operating costs rise, increasing pressures are placed on councils to maintain the quality and breadth of library collections, digital services and community programming, creating service and financial risks across the sector.
 
  1. Supports the LGA South Australia’s advocacy position which requests increased funding for libraries.
 
  1. Supports the City of Charles Sturt's contribution to a coordinated sector approach, led by the LGA SA.
 
  1. Provides public support for the LGA South Australia’s position to seek annual CPI increases on a new multi-year funding agreement with the State Government, noting that current state funding for public libraries has not kept pace with rising costs and service demand over a number of years.
 
  1. Seeks opportunities to meet with and advocate to local Members or Parliament, working with the LGA SA.
 
  1. Endorses the Mayor and CEO to sign LGA SA advocacy communications to achieve the above.
 
  1. That Strategic and Engagement Committee ask admin staff to make a submission for the National Cultural Policy on behalf of the City of Charles Sturt if feasible.
 
 
4.2. - PRESENTATION - CLIMATE CHANGE RESPONSE PLAN UPDATE 
 
Motion
 
That the Committee recommends that
 
  1. Council receive and note the update on the implementation of the Climate Change Response Plan 2024–2030.
 
 
4.3. - PRESENTATION - HOME ENERGY UPGRADE REBATE PROGRAM
 
Motion
 
 That the Committee recommends that Council:
 
  1. Receives and notes the presentation and overview of the proposed Home Energy Upgrade Rebate Program.
 
  1. Endorses the implementation of the Home Energy Upgrade Rebates Program – Tier 1 Pilot, as outlined in this report, to be delivered in 2026/27.
 
  1. Endorses the associated Program Guidelines for the Tier 1 Pilot, as provided in Appendix 2.
 
  1. Notes that future program expansion phases (Tier 2 and Tier 3) will be subject to separate reports and further Council consideration.
  
4.5. - TRANSFER OF LAND OWNERSHIP - LOT 1001 WOODVILLE ROAD, WOODVILLE
 
Motion
 
That the Committee recommends that
 
  1. Council accepts the transfer of ownership of Allotment 1001 in Deposited Plan 116180 shown in Certificate of Title Volume 6224 Folio 99.
 
  1. Council delegates authority to the Mayor and Chief Executive Officer to sign, seal and deal with all documents to deliver the transfer of ownership.


 

Council adopts the recommendations of the Committee as printed in the Minutes of this Committee, and that Councillor McEwen be included as an apology for the meeting.


Carried Unanimously


Moved: Councillor Rachele Tullio
Seconded: Councillor Kelly Thomas

4.4. - SEATON CODE AMENDMENT - MINISTERIAL ADOPTION
 
Motion
 
 That the Committee recommends to Council:
 
  1. That Council acknowledges the adoption of the Seaton Code Amendment by the Minister for Planning, noting the amendment does not align with Council's feedback.

  2. That further work done via the City Plan reflects Council's feedback to the State Government on the Seaton Code Amendment.

  3. That Council be included in future dialogues regarding Code Amendments, and that the Mayor and CEO meet with the Minister to provide feedback.
Carried

The Operations Committee was held on Monday, 18 May2026.


Moved: Councillor Edgar Agius
Seconded: Councillor Senthil Chidambaranathan

That having considered the recommendations of the Committee which has read and considered the reports in the agenda related to items:

 

4.1. - VERGE MOWING PROGRAM - PROPOSED ADDITIONAL LOCAL ROADS CUT
 
Motion 
 
 That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That Council endorses the proposed variation to the verge mowing program to introduce an additional mowing cut for local roads, increasing the service level from five to six cuts per year, and a corresponding reduction in the main roads mowing program from eight to seven cuts per year, as outlined in this report, to better balance service delivery outcomes across the City.
 
  1. That Council notes that this service level variation will be managed within the overall verge management budget.
 
4.2. - SOUTH AUSTRALIAN FOOTBALL FACILITIES FUND - FUNDING ACCEPTANCE
 
That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That this item be deferred to the Council meeting on 25 May 2026 due to want of quorum. 
 
4.3. - CITY OPERATIONS CAPITAL WORKS & OPERATING PROGRAM VARIATIONS
 
Motion 
 
 That the Committee recommends to the Council: 
 
  1. That the following variations to the Capital Works Program or Annual Operating Program be approved and adjusted in the budget and annual financial statements 2025/26 as they involve transfers between renewal and new/upgrade works and or new projects to be funded by unbudgeted income: 
     
     a. Budgeted expenditure for Road Reconstruction Program 2025/26 Seaview Road - K&G Renewal (Project 3731 - Renewal) be increased by $825,000 for additional funding required, comprising:
     
     - $400,000 from unspent budget within the Road Reconstruction Program 2025/26 Contingency (Project 3724 - Renewal),
     - $100,000 consolidated from the Water Conveyance Assets - New and Upgrade Seaview Road (Project 3877 - Upgrade),
     - $300,000 from savings identified within the Path and Access Ramp Renewals 25/26 (Project 3776 - Renewal), and
     - $25,000 transferred from the Bus Stop Renewals 25/26 (Project 3697 - Renewal).
     
     b. Budgeted expenditure for Playground Shade Structures 2025/26 (Project 3851 - New) be increased by $170,000 from reallocated funds within the Bridge Renewal - Seaview Road Underpass RTLP (Project 3623 - Renewal), to enable the Grange Shade Sail replacement to be completed.
     
     c. Budgeted expenditure for AMP Irrigation Renewals 2025/26 (Project 3841 - Renewal) be increased by $48,000 from Parkway Reserve Additional Landscaping (Project 3594 - New), for additional funding required.
     
     d. Budgeted expenditure for the Woodville South Cricket Club - Cricket Nets (Project 3638 - New) be increased by $100,000 from Woodville South Football Club Changerooms (Project 3614 - Upgrade), for additional funding required.

  2. That the following variations to the Capital Works Program be approved and budgets or scope adjusted accordingly:
     
     a.  That Parkway Reserve Irrigation (Project 3691 - New) and Parkway Reserve - Additional Landscaping (Project 3594 - New) be consolidated into a single project line for ease of reporting and tracking.

  3.  That by endorsing the variations listed in 1. above, Council is endorsing a variation to the approved Asset Management Plan renewal schedule where relevant.
 
4.4. - COAST PARK STAGE TWO (GRANGE TO TENNYSON) - PROJECT UPDATE 
 
Motion 
 
 That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That Council notes the update on the Coast Park Stage Two Project, between Grange and Tennyson.
 
  1. That Council acknowledges construction is anticipated to commence later in 2026, with ongoing progress reports to be provided to Council during the construction phase.
 
4.5. - ST CLAIR RECREATION CENTRE QUARTERLY REPORT - JANUARY, FEBRUARY AND MARCH 2026
 
Motion 
 
 That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That Council notes the YMCA's Performance Report for the January to March 2026 quarter. 

  2. That further quarterly reports be presented to the Operations Committee.
 
4.6. - STREETSCAPE UPGRADE PROJECTS - QUARTERLY UPDATE REPORT
 
Motion 
 
 That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That the report be received and noted. 
 
  1. That Council notes that grant applications have been submitted to the Safer Local Roads and Infrastructure Program ($3 million) and the State Bicycle Fund ($200,000) to support the delivery outcomes of the Chief Street Project.

 

Council adopts the recommendations of the Committee as printed in the Minutes of this Committee.


[NOTE: Item 4.2 was deferred to Council. Refer to Item 6.1 of this agenda] 
Carried Unanimously

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Brief

This report seeks Council approval for a $2.5 million capital investment in solar photovoltaic (PV) systems and battery energy storage systems (BESS) across Council-owned sporting and community club facilities as part of the next stage of the Community Renewables Program.

The report also outlines the relationship between this initiative and the ongoing review of the Sporting & Community Clubs Fees Policy following significant increases in facility valuations and the resulting financial implications for tenant clubs under the current fee model. 



Moved: Councillor Michael McEwen
Seconded: Councillor Peter Ppiros

Motion

That Council:

  1. Support the inclusion of $2.5 million in capital funding within the draft 2026/27 Budget, for consideration through the Corporate Services Committee and subsequent Council budget adoption process, to deliver the next tranche of the Community Renewables Program through the installation of solar photovoltaic (PV) systems and battery energy storage systems (BESS) across Council-owned sporting and community club facilities.

  2. Note that this investment will:
    • deliver approximately 800kW of solar PV generation capacity and 1.7MWh of battery storage;
    • deliver an average 25% reduction in electricity costs for participating sporting and community clubs through a fixed electricity charging framework designed to provide long-term price certainty;
    • deliver cumulative annual electricity cost savings of approximately $97,850 for participating sporting and community clubs; and
    • reduce the administrative burden on club treasurers associated with managing electricity retailer agreements and energy costs.

  3. Note that following the 2024/2025 revaluation of Council-owned sporting and community club facilities, application of the current Sporting & Community Clubs Fees Policy would have resulted in significant increases in tenancy fees for a number of clubs and associations, and that Council has continued, and will continue, to apply fee arrangements based on pre-2024 valuation outcomes until completion of a future review of the Sporting & Community Clubs Fees Policy.

  4. Note that the Community Renewables Program is intended to establish a revised operating cost baseline for clubs through reduced electricity costs prior to Council considering future Sporting & Community Clubs Fees Policy options.

  5. Request that a separate report and workshop be presented to Council reviewing future Sporting & Community Clubs Fees Policy options, including alternative fee model approaches informed by:
    • updated asset valuations;
    • operating cost reductions achieved through the renewable energy initiative;
    • the historic equity arrangements embedded within the current policy framework; and
    • Council’s objective of maintaining financially sustainable and community-accessible sporting and community organisations.


Carried
