To seek Council endorsement of the Draft Community Engagement Policy and supporting Community Engagement Approach to enable community consultation, with a further report to be presented to Council prior to the caretaker period to finalise the policy.



Moved: Councillor Katriona Kinsella


Councillor - Rachele Tullio left the meeting at 8:21 PM.

Seconded: Councillor Stuart Ghent

For the Council to consider a presentation from the Chief Executive Officer (CEO) on achievements against the agreed objectives for the financial year 2025/26. External consultant, Allison Ashby of AM Consulting has been engaged to assist in conducting the review, and will be in attendance at the meeting to provide an overview and timeline of this year's process enabling Elected Members to complete a confidential survey to provide feedback in relation to the CEO's performance for the previous 12 months.

In accordance with the Local Government Act 1999 the CEO is recommending that this report be heard in confidence under Section 90(3)(a) as the information the disclosure of which would involve the unreasonable disclosure of information concerning the personal affairs of a person or persons (living or dead).



Moved: Councillor Edgar AgiusSeconded: Councillor Michael McEwen

Recommendation - Exclusion of the Public (from 8:42 PM)
That:
  1. Pursuant to Section 90(2) of the Local Government Act 1999, Council hereby orders that the public be excluded from attendance at this meeting, with the exception of the Chief Executive Officer, General Manager Engaged Community, General Manager Corporate Services, General Manager City Operations, General Manager City Futures, Manager City Infrastructure, Manager City Utilities, Manager City Property and Open Space, Manager Community Connections, Manager City Planning and Sustainability, Manager Community Engagement and Experience, Manager People and Culture, Manager Performance, Business Intelligence and Improvement, Acting Manager Governance and Risk, Coordinator Sustainability Strategy, Governance Officer, and Allison Ashby (AM Consulting) currently in attendance at the meeting, in order to consider ITEM 11.1 CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER PRESENTATION FOR PERFORMANCE REVIEW 2025/26 in confidence.

  2. In accordance with Section 90(3) of the Local Government Act 1999, Council is satisfied that it is necessary that the public be excluded to consider the information contained in the report ITEM 11.1 CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER PRESENTATION FOR PERFORMANCE REVIEW 2025/26 on the following grounds:
a.
information the disclosure of which would involve the unreasonable disclosure of information concerning the personal affairs of a person or persons (living or dead).

Recommended Action
  1. Accordingly, on this basis, the principle that meetings of the Council should be conducted in a place open to the public has been outweighed by the need to keep the information or discussion confidential.


Councillor - Katriona Kinsella left the meeting at 8:42 PM.

Carried Unanimously

Councillor - Kelly Thomas left the meeting at 8:42 PM.
Councillor - Katriona Kinsella entered the meeting at 8:43 PM.
Councillor - Kelly Thomas entered the meeting at 8:44 PM.


Moved: Councillor Senthil ChidambaranathanSeconded: Councillor Edgar Agius

Motion

That Council continue past 9 PM and adjourn for a break at the conclusion of Item 11.1, in accordance with the Code of Practice for Meeting Procedures.
Carried Unanimously

Councillor - Nicole Mazeika left the meeting at 9:21 PM.

Councillor - Nicole Mazeika entered the meeting at 9:24 PM.


Moved: Councillor Nicole MazeikaSeconded: Councillor Senthil Chidambaranathan

Motion

  1. That the Council accepts the presentation provided by the CEO on the achievements against the agreed objectives (Key Performance Indicators (refer Appendix 2)) as outlined in the Performance Review Plan for 2025/2026.

  2. That Elected Members consider the achievements of the CEO and provide feedback by way of a survey provided by AM Consulting.

  3. That a further report be presented to Council on 24 August 2026 reflecting the outcomes of the CEO Performance Review which will include 360 degree feedback from Elected Members, staff and external stakeholders, and any other relevant matters in order to finalise the CEO’s Performance Review.

  4. That the objectives (Key Performance Indicators) developed by the Mayor and CEO for the 2026/27 year be approved by the CEO Review Panel for the integration into a Performance Review Plan, with the assistance from the appointed Consultant.
 
  1. That ITEM 11.1 – CHIEF EXECUTIVE OFFICER PRESENTATION FOR PERFORMANCE REVIEW 2025/26 having been considered in confidence pursuant to Section 90(3)(a) of the Local Government Act 1999, the Council hereby orders, in accordance with Section 91(7) of the Local Government Act 1999 that the report, appendices and minutes be kept confidential until after the final review report is brought back to Council at the meeting of Monday, 24 August 2026.

 


Carried Unanimously


Moved: Councillor Rachele TullioSeconded: Councillor Katriona Kinsella

Adjournment - 9:35 PM
That Council adjourn for a 10 minute break in accordance with the Code of Practice for Meeting Procedures.
Carried Unanimously


Moved: Councillor Edgar AgiusSeconded: Councillor Stuart Ghent

Resumption - 9:45 PM

That Council resume.

Carried Unanimously

At the resumption of the meeting Councillor Katriona Kinsella and Councillor - Nicholas Le Lacheur were not present.

The Strategic and Engagement Committee was held on Monday, 18 May 2026 and considered Item 9.1 Presentation - Potential Acquisition and Activation of Local Heritage Building in Kilkenny. The brief of this item is provided as follows:

To seek Council endorsement for Administration to undertake further investigations and commence preliminary negotiations regarding a potential strategic property opportunity within the Kilkenny area.

The Strategic and Engagement Committee was held on Monday, 18 May 2026 and considered Item 9.3 Henley Beach Precinct - Council Owned Properties. The brief of this item is provided as follows:

This report presents considerations relating to two Council-owned properties within the Henley Beach precinct and seeks endorsement to undertake a coordinated Expression of Interest (EOI) process relating to the future of both sites. The report also seeks Council endorsement of a set of guiding principles to inform the assessment of future proposals.

In accordance with the Local Government Act 1999 the CEO is recommending that this report be heard in confidence under Section 90(3)(b) as it contains information the disclosure of which (i) could reasonably be expected to confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting, or proposing to conduct, business, or to prejudice the commercial position of the council; and (ii) would, on balance, be contrary to the public interest.



Moved: Councillor Edgar Agius
Seconded: Councillor Michael McEwen

Recommendation - Exclusion of the Public (from 10:13 PM)
That:
  1. Pursuant to Section 90(2) of the Local Government Act 1999, Council hereby orders that the public be excluded from attendance at this meeting, with the exception of the Chief Executive Officer, General Manager Engaged Community, General Manager Corporate Services, General Manager City Operations, General Manager City Futures, Manager City Infrastructure, Manager City Utilities, Manager City Property and Open Space, Manager Community Connections, Manager City Planning and Sustainability, Acting Manager Governance and Risk, Coordinator Sustainability Strategy, and Governance Officer currently in attendance at the meeting, in order to consider ITEM 12.3 - STRATEGIC AND ENGAGEMENT COMMITTEE - ITEM 9.3 HENLEY BEACH PRECINCT - COUNCIL OWNED PROPERTIES  in confidence.

  2. In accordance with Section 90(3) of the Local Government Act 1999, Council is satisfied that it is necessary that the public be excluded to consider the information contained in the report ITEM 12.3 - STRATEGIC AND ENGAGEMENT COMMITTEE - ITEM 9.3 HENLEY BEACH PRECINCT - COUNCIL OWNED PROPERTIES on the following grounds:

b.
information the disclosure of which (i) could reasonably be expected to confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting, or proposing to conduct, business, or to prejudice the commercial position of the council; and (ii) would, on balance, be contrary to the public interest.

Recommended Action
  1. Accordingly, on this basis, the principle that meetings of the Council should be conducted in a place open to the public has been outweighed by the need to keep the information or discussion confidential.
Carried Unanimously


Moved: Councillor Kenzie van den Nieuwelaar
Seconded: Councillor Kelly Thomas

  1. That having considered the recommendation of the Committee which has read and considered the report in the agenda related to item:

9.3 HENLEY BEACH PRECINCT - COUNCIL OWNED PROPERTIES

Motion

  1. That Council endorse the release of two concurrent Expressions of Interest (EOI) processes for the properties located at 136 North Street, Henley Beach, and 196A Military Road, Henley Beach, inviting submissions for all potential future opportunities, including but not limited to future land use, site activation, tenure and leasing arrangements, and partnership models.

  2. That Council endorse the Guiding Principles outlined in Attachment 1 for inclusion within the Expression of Interest (EOI) documentation and to guide the assessment of submissions received through the process, subject to the following addition: 
    1. that existing established community groups in the City of Charles Sturt be given priority consideration.

  3. That a further report be presented to Council following completion of the EOI process outlining submissions received, together with recommended next steps.

  4. That ITEM 9.3 HENLEY BEACH PRECINCT - COUNCIL OWNED PROPERTIES having been considered in confidence pursuant to Section 90(3)(b)(i) and (ii) of the Local Government Act 1999, the Strategic and Engagement Committee hereby orders, in accordance with Section 91(7) of the Local Government Act 1999 that the appendices 2 and 3 of this item be kept confidential until a decision has been made relative to each EOI process.

Carried

A Question on Notice has been received from Councillor Senthil Chidambaranathan in relation to traffic queuing and safety concerns at the Park Street South / Port Road intersection.


Questions

Can the administration please provide:

  1. An update on the status of the community consultation process undertaken in relation to the Park Street South traffic queuing issue.

  2. A summary of the feedback received from residents, businesses, and stakeholders on the proposed options.

  3. Details of any preferred option currently being considered by the Administration.

  4. The anticipated timeline for a report and/or recommendation to be presented to Council for consideration; and

  5. Advice on whether any interim traffic management or safety measures are proposed pending a final decision.


Questions and Answers

Can the administration please provide:

1. An update on the status of the community consultation process undertaken in relation to the Park Street South traffic queuing issue.
Council undertook community consultation between 15 July 2025 and 5 August 2025 regarding several potential traffic management treatments to address vehicle queuing associated with the First Things First café drive-through on Park Street South.

The consultation process has now concluded and Administration has reviewed the feedback received from residents, businesses and stakeholders. Following consideration of the consultation outcomes, Administration has determined to proceed with Option 3, which involved no major infrastructure changes, supported by minor parking control amendments and continued engagement with the business regarding operational management of vehicle queuing.

2. A summary of the feedback received from residents, businesses, and stakeholders on the proposed options.
Feedback received through the consultation process reflected a range of views from residents, businesses and road users.

Key themes raised included:
  • concerns regarding ongoing morning peak traffic queuing and congestion on Park Street South
  • safety concerns relating to driver behaviour, visibility and turning movements
  • impacts on local business access and customer convenience
  • concerns regarding possible traffic redistribution onto surrounding local streets
  • mixed views regarding the proposed median treatments and left-in/left-out access arrangements, with some respondents supporting stronger intervention measures while others expressed concern regarding access restrictions and impacts on local traffic circulation.

Overall, feedback indicated limited consensus within the community regarding more significant traffic infrastructure changes.

3. Details of any preferred option currently being considered by the Administration.
We have determined to proceed with Option 3, involving:
  • no major intersection or roadway infrastructure changes
  • implementation of revised parking time limits adjacent to the business to support short-term, high-turnover parking associated with coffee collection
  • ongoing discussions with the business regarding operational management practices aimed at minimising vehicle queuing impacts on the surrounding road network.

The revised parking controls have now been implemented.

4. The anticipated timeline for a report and/or recommendation to be presented to Council for consideration; and
As the matter has been addressed administratively through the implementation of revised parking controls and ongoing operational discussions with the business, no further Council report is currently scheduled at this time. We will continue to monitor conditions at the location and will provide further advice to Council should additional intervention measures become necessary in the future.

5. Advice on whether any interim traffic management or safety measures are proposed pending a final decision.
The revised parking time limits adjacent to the business have now been implemented to support improved turnover of customer parking spaces and assist in managing short-duration pick-up activity associated with the café. We will continue to monitor traffic conditions and liaise with the business regarding operational management of queuing activity.

Separately, Council is also currently working with the Department for Infrastructure and Transport (DIT) regarding investigations into safety improvements associated with the Port Road / Oval Avenue intersection black spot. While this is a separate project, any future changes arising from these investigations may potentially provide broader traffic operation benefits within the surrounding road network, including the Park Street South area.

Questions on Notice have been received from Councillor - Senthil Chidambaranathan in relation to Cheltenham Racecourse anti-social behaviour.


Questions

  1. Following reports of rubbish, broken glass and incidents involving human faeces within the children’s soft play area, has Council undertaken a hygiene or public health assessment of the playground infrastructure? 

  2. Will the Administration consider replacing or redesigning affected soft play elements with infrastructure that is safer, more hygienic, and easier to maintain for children and families? 

  3. Can the Administration provide an update on any additional measures being considered with SAPOL and other agencies to reduce ongoing anti-social behaviour and improve community safety within the reserve precinct? 

  4. Are there any plans to increase the frequency of cleaning, inspections or monitoring of the playground and surrounding reserve during periods of recurring anti-social behaviour? 

  5. What lessons has Council learnt from managing this situation, and how will those learnings inform future responses to similar issues in other reserves, playgrounds, or public spaces across the City of Charles Sturt?


Questions and Answers

  1. Following reports of rubbish, broken glass and incidents involving human faeces within the children’s soft play area, has Council undertaken a hygiene or public health assessment of the playground infrastructure? 

Administration acknowledges community concerns regarding hygiene and amenity within the playground area at Cheltenham Racecourse Reserve following recent incidents.

 

In response to reports of litter, broken glass and other hygiene-related issues, staff undertook an immediate and coordinated operational response, crossing over Engaged Community Division and City Operations Division. Actions as part of this response included a forensic-level clean of the playground and surrounding infrastructure by a specialised contractor, as well as the removal of litter and hazardous materials such as broken glass.

 

In addition to these works, the site has been subject to ongoing inspections and monitoring by Council staff across City Clean, Community Safety and Parks teams. These inspections have focused on identifying and addressing any hygiene or safety risks, with hazards promptly removed and the site maintained to support safe public use.

 

The combination of specialist cleaning, routine safety inspections and proactive hazard management provides assurance that the playground infrastructure remains safe, compliant and suitable for continued community use. Administration will continue to monitor the site and respond as required.

 

  1. Will the Administration consider replacing or redesigning affected soft play elements with infrastructure that is safer, more hygienic, and easier to maintain for children and families?

We acknowledge the community concerns raised regarding hygiene and amenity within the playground area at Cheltenham Racecourse Reserve following recent incidents of anti-social behaviour. Following the reports, Council undertook a coordinated response which included a deep clean of the playground and associated public infrastructure by a specialised contractor. This included the rubber soft-fall areas, pathways, BBQ shelters, picnic settings and associated surfaces. Ongoing proactive inspections and cleaning arrangements have also been implemented.

 

The playground was independently inspected on 4 February 2026 as part of Council’s scheduled Level 3 playground safety inspection program. The inspection confirmed that the playground equipment and surfacing generally remain in satisfactory condition and compliant for continued use, with only routine maintenance and soft-fall top-up works identified.

 

We will continue to monitor the condition, performance and maintenance requirements of playground soft-fall surfaces across the City as part of future asset renewal planning. At this stage, there are no immediate plans to fully replace the existing soft-fall materials at this site. However, officers have considered alternative surfacing treatments and note that current rubber and engineered woodchip surfaces remain the industry standard across local government due to their balance of safety performance, accessibility, maintainability and lifecycle cost.

 

Council officers have also investigated alternative surfacing products and hybrid systems. While smoother sealed surfaces may provide some cleaning advantages, they can also introduce other considerations including increased surface heat during summer conditions, higher installation costs and differing maintenance requirements. As part of ongoing playground asset management planning, staff will continue to assess opportunities to improve durability, hygiene outcomes, accessibility and ease of maintenance when future renewal or upgrade works are programmed for this reserve and other playground sites across the City.

 

  1. Can the Administration provide an update on any additional measures being considered with SAPOL and other agencies to reduce ongoing anti-social behaviour and improve community safety within the reserve precinct? 

We are continuing to work closely with SAPOL and a range of partner agencies to support community safety throughout the City of Charles Sturt, and in particular at this location currently.

 

A coordinated, cross-agency response has been established involving SAPOL, the Department of Human Services (DHS) Remote Visitors Outreach team, and multiple Council teams. This approach includes regular information sharing, joint site monitoring, and coordinated outreach to individuals accessing areas in the City of Charles Sturt including the Cheltenham Racecourse Reserve.

 

SAPOL have increased patrol activity within the area, particularly during peak periods, and remain engaged in monitoring and responding to incidents as required. Council officers maintain regular communication with SAPOL and DHS to ensure emerging risks are identified early and appropriate responses are coordinated.

 

Alongside enforcement and monitoring, the response has prioritised connecting individuals with appropriate support services, including health, housing and Return to Country programs. This coordinated and balanced approach aims to improve safety and amenity within the reserve while supporting vulnerable members of the community. In addition, our Community Development team is coordinating positive activations within the space, including a ‘Pot Painting in the Park’ activity on Saturday 30 May, to support a safe, welcoming and family-friendly environment.

 

Further, Council has installed additional signage within and around the playground to reinforce expected behaviours. This includes reminders that smoking is prohibited within 10 metres of children’s playground, as well as broader messaging promoting respectful use of the space.

 

We will continue to work with partner agencies and implement targeted measures to support safe and respectful use of the reserve and respond to changing circumstances at the site.

 

  1. Are there any plans to increase the frequency of cleaning, inspections or monitoring of the playground and surrounding reserve during periods of recurring anti-social behaviour? 

Maintaining a high standard of cleanliness, safety and amenity within public spaces is incredibly important, particularly during periods of increased use or reported anti-social behaviour.

In response to recent activity, Council has implemented increased cleaning, inspection and monitoring arrangements across the playground and surrounding reserve. This has included daily proactive cleaning of the site, supplemented by reactive cleaning as required, as well as regular site inspections and monitoring by City Clean, Community Safety and Parks teams.

 

These measures have been supported by coordinated internal communication and reporting processes, ensuring that hazards such as waste, broken glass and other debris are identified and addressed promptly to maintain safe conditions for the community.

 

We will continue to adjust the frequency and intensity of cleaning, inspections and monitoring in response to changing conditions, with a flexible approach that ensures resources are targeted to areas and times of greatest need.

 

This approach will also inform ongoing operational planning for similar situations across other reserves and public spaces within the City.

 

  1. What lessons has Council learnt from managing this situation, and how will those learnings inform future responses to similar issues in other reserves, playgrounds, or public spaces across the City of Charles Sturt?

We have applied a coordinated, place-based approach in responding to the situation at Cheltenham Racecourse Reserve, building on learnings from previous responses to similar issues, including the Ovingham underpass.

 

These experiences have reinforced the importance of early, sustained and coordinated collaboration across Council teams and with external agencies. Establishing strong partnerships with SAPOL, DHS and community services has enabled a proactive, whole-of-system response that brings together monitoring, outreach and service coordination.

 

A key learning from both Ovingham and Cheltenham is the value of an integrated approach that combines operational responses, such as cleaning, inspections and maintenance, with community development practices focused on engagement, relationship-building and connecting people to appropriate supports.

 

Council’s regulatory role is supported by a graduated approach to compliance, working in partnership with relevant agencies and guided by enforcement principles that prioritise education and encouragement before escalation where required.

 

The response has also reinforced the importance of maintaining a consistent presence on site and taking a measured, proportionate approach that can adapt to changing circumstances. This includes prioritising early intervention, ongoing monitoring and shared intelligence across agencies, rather than relying solely on reactive or enforcement-based measures.

 

Importantly, this approach reflects an ongoing cycle of learning and adaptation. We continue to refine its response model based on experience, strengthening cross-agency coordination, internal processes and operational practices to ensure responses to similar situations across the City are timely, consistent and balanced, supporting both community safety and the wellbeing of vulnerable individuals.”

Questions on Notice have been received from Councillor Senthil Chidambaranathan in relation to parking concerns raised by St Clair residents.


Questions

Following the parking concerns raised by St Clair residents over recent weekends regarding illegal parking, including vehicles parking on verges and nature strips, blocking residential driveways, and creating safety and access issues, can the Administration advise:

  1. What actions are planned by Council to address these ongoing parking concerns during periods of high sporting involving sporting clubs and school-related activity in the St Clair area?

  1. Will Council consider allocating a dedicated Parking Inspector or additional compliance resources during peak weekend activity periods?

  1. Will Council communicate with participating schools, sporting clubs, and user groups to remind patrons, players and visitors to comply with parking restrictions and Australian Road Rules to avoid expiation notices and minimise inconvenience to residents?

  1. Are there any longer-term traffic or parking management measures being considered to improve compliance and reduce the impact on surrounding residents?


Questions and Answers

Following the parking concerns raised by St Clair residents over recent weekends regarding illegal parking, including vehicles parking on verges and nature strips, blocking residential driveways, and creating safety and access issues, can the Administration advise:

  1. What actions are planned by Council to address these ongoing parking concerns during periods of high sporting involving sporting clubs and school-related activity in the St Clair area?
Council’s after-hours service operates at a reduced level relative to standard business hours and is prioritised based on safety risks and service standards. To address ongoing parking concerns in the St Clair area, Council undertakes targeted patrols of identified high-demand locations during periods of peak sporting and school-related activity including in surrounding the ovals at St Clair. In addition, patrol routes and deployment are informed by known demand patterns and community feedback to ensure resources are directed to areas of greatest impact. These actions aim to provide a visible enforcement presence, support compliance, and respond to safety-related issues as they arise.

 

  1. Will Council consider allocating a dedicated Parking Inspector or additional compliance resources during peak weekend activity periods?
Council could consider allocating additional compliance resources during peak weekend activity periods. Any allocation would need to be assessed in the context of established after-hours service levels, available budget, and existing staffing resources to ensure an equitable and sustainable approach across our City.

  1. Will Council communicate with participating schools, sporting clubs, and user groups to remind patrons, players and visitors to comply with parking restrictions and Australian Road Rules to avoid expiation notices and minimise inconvenience to residents?
Yes. Council staff will circulate parking maps and compliance information through the NWJSA to all participating schools, as well as to other sporting clubs and user groups that access the precinct. Communication will remind patrons, players and visitors of the importance of complying with parking restrictions and Australian Road Rules to help avoid expiation notices and minimise impacts on surrounding residents.

Staff are continually exploring new and innovative ways to better communicate with and educate our community and have been progressing a campaign designed to educate the community and visitors on appropriate parking within the City of Charles Sturt. 

  1. Are there any longer-term traffic or parking management measures being considered to improve compliance and reduce the impact on surrounding residents?
Council is currently considering a range of longer-term traffic and parking management measures as part of the broader St Clair Recreation Precinct planning process. A detailed traffic and parking study was undertaken and identified several opportunities to improve parking capacity, traffic circulation, and overall compliance within the precinct, as part of the upcoming works. These measures include reconfiguring existing indented parking bays along St Clair Avenue from parallel to 45-degree angled parking, as well as constructing a new off-street car park adjacent to Oval 2. Collectively, the broader precinct improvements are projected to deliver an additional 138 parking spaces across the area, helping to reduce congestion and parking impacts on surrounding residential streets during peak periods. Council has allocated funding within the draft 2026/27 Budget to support the delivery of these works.

This report provides Council with an update on early research and analysis undertaken by Administration to better understand the current and future delivery of the City of Charles Sturt’s 3 Bin Kerbside Waste Collection Service. This work was initiated in response to known service performance issues, increasing market pressures and the need to ensure Council is prepared for future decisions about this essential service. No decision is sought to change the current service delivery model at this time. This report seeks Council’s support to progress further due diligence, engagement and planning before any future service delivery recommendation is brought back for consideration.

In accordance with the Local Government Act 1999 the CEO is recommending that this report be heard in confidence under Section 90(3)(b) as information the disclosure of which (i) could reasonably be expected to confer a commercial advantage on a person with whom the council is conducting, or proposing to conduct, business, or to prejudice the commercial position of the council; and (ii) would, on balance, be contrary to the public interest.

The Corporate Services Committee was held on Monday, 1 June 2026.


Moved: Councillor Alice CampbellSeconded: Councillor Nicholas Le Lacheur

That having considered the recommendations of the Committee which has read and considered the reports in the agenda related to all items, with the exception of Items 4.2, 4.3 and 4.4:

 

4.1. - PRESENTATION - COMMUNITY RENEWABLES UPDATE
 
Motion 
 
That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That the report be received and noted.
 
  1. That Council note the continued delivery of Council’s renewable energy initiatives through:
    1. the Community Renewables residential bulk-buy and Virtual Power Plant (VPP) program;
    2. the long-term renewable energy contract agreement with Flow Power;
    3. installation of battery energy storage systems and associated solar infrastructure at Council operational sites; 
    4. the VPP Revenue Share Agreement;
    5. the Home Energy Upgrade Rebate Program; and 
    6. the proposed Sporting and Community Clubs Renewable Energy Program, subject to consideration through the 2026/27 budget process.
 
  1. That staff be thanked for their presentation and that a copy of the presentation be included in the Minutes.
 
4.5. - REVIEW OF THE FEES & CHARGES REGISTER 2026/27
 
Motion 
 
That the Committee recommend to Council:
 
  1. That pursuant to Section 188 of the Local Government Act 1999, Council adopt the schedule of fees and charges detailed in Appendix 1 to the report, effective 1 July 2026.
  2. That the schedule be prepared as Council's Fees and Charges Register for publication on Council's website and be subject to annual review.
  
4.6. - ANCILLARY INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS - CARRY FORWARD FUNDING REQUEST FOR 2026/2027
 
Motion 
 
That the Committee recommend to Council:
 
  1. That Council reviews and endorses the carry forward of unspent 2025/26 Ancillary Infrastructure funding into the 2026/27 financial year for the following projects, to enable their continued successful delivery:
  1. Flinders Park Tennis Club - Court Upgrade
  2. Seaside Tennis Club - Court Upgrades
  3. Pennington Oval - Sports Lighting Upgrade
 
4.7. - POLICY REVIEW - SISTER CITY RELATIONSHIP 
 
Motion
 
That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That Council revokes the existing Sister City Relationship Policy.
 
  1. That Council notes that any future international engagement opportunities are able to be explored and considered by Council on a case-by-case basis where there is a clear community benefit.
 
  1. That Council writes to each Sister and Friendship City partner organisation to:
  • Acknowledge the history and value of the relationship;
  • Advise that Council has recently undertaken a review of its international partnerships and current arrangements; and 
  • Communicate Council’s intention to formally conclude the Sister and Friendship City agreement in a respectful and orderly manner, while noting that Council remains open to considering future engagement opportunities on a case-by-case basis where there is clear strategic value.
 
4.8. - POLICY REVIEW - SOCIAL INCLUSION POLICY
 
Motion
  
That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That Council adopts the Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Policy as presented at Attachment 1, effective from the date of this resolution; and
  2. Notes that the Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Policy supersedes the Social Inclusion Policy (Policy 4.36, last reviewed October 2024).
 
4.9. - POLICIES FOR REVIEW - MINOR CHANGES ONLY
 
Motion
  
That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That the Development Act 1993 Delegations Policy (Appendix 1) be revoked.
 
  1. That the revised Parking Controls Policy (Appendix 2) be adopted.
  

Council adopts the recommendations of the Committee as printed in the Minutes of this Committee.

Carried Unanimously


Moved: Councillor Alice CampbellSeconded: Councillor Nicholas Le Lacheur

4.2. - DRAFT ANNUAL BUSINESS PLAN CONSULTATION RESULTS 2026/27
 
Motion
 
That the Committee recommends to Council that:
 
  1. That the report be received and noted.
 
Carried Unanimously


Moved: Councillor Alice CampbellSeconded: Councillor Nicholas Le Lacheur

4.3. - PROPOSED RECURRENT BUDGET AND LIST OF CAPITAL AND ANNUAL OPERATING PROJECTS FOR 2026/27
 
Motion
 
That the Committee recommend to Council:
 
  1. That the report be received and noted.
 
  1. That the Council consider the following recommendations from the Corporate Services Committee as part of ﬁnalising the 2026/27 Budget.
 
Carried 

Councillor - Katriona Kinsella left the meeting at 7:43 PM.
Councillor - Katriona Kinsella entered the meeting at 7:47 PM.



Moved: Councillor Alice CampbellSeconded: Councillor Nicholas Le Lacheur

Motion
 
  1. That the Capital Renewal Projects totalling $26,361,302 in expenditure and $0 in associated income for a net $26,361,302 as set out in Appendix 1 be provided for in the 2026/27 Budget, noting that the 2027/28 Capital Renewal Program is increased by $754k, and noting that scope and budget adjustments have been made to projects based on community consultation and further staff feedback including:
    1. PBB-00002543 Inlet Reserve Renewal Public Amenities, the expenditure budget to be reduced by $550k ($600k down to $50k), with $550k being deferred to the 2027/28 financial year. 
    2. PBB-00002508 Heavy Fleet Replacement Program 26/27, the expenditure budget reduced by $204k ($3,101,995 down to $2,897,995), with $204k being deferred to the 2027/28 financial year. 

Carried 


Moved: Councillor Alice CampbellSeconded: Councillor Peter Ppiros

Motion
 
  1. That the Capital New and Upgrade Projects totalling $32,611,311 in expenditure and $2,235,625 in associated income for a net expenditure of $30,357,686 as set out in Appendix 2 to the report, be provided for in the 2026/27 Budget, noting that $5.075m be deferred to the 2027/28 financial year and noting that scope adjustments have been made to 2026/27 projects based on community consultation and further staff feedback including:
    1. PBB-00002545 Grange Bowling Club Acquisition and Upgrade, the $5.7m project has been removed.
    2. PBB-00002538 Trimmer Parade Stormwater Drainage Renewal - Stages 1 & 2 Construction, the expenditure budget to be reduced by $3.175m ($6,175,000 down to $3,000,000), with $3.175m being deferred to the 2027/28 financial year. Income to be increased for 2026/27 to $1.4m (pending a future Council report).
    3. PBB-00002561 Beverley Depot Redevelopment - Construction 2026/27, the expenditure budget to be reduced by $1.5m ($2.0m down to $500k), with $1.5m being deferred to the 2027/28 financial year.
    4. PBB-00002560 Inlet Reserve – Inclusive Play Space Development, the project to be removed from the 2026/27 budget and the project and expenditure budget of $400k to be deferred to the 2027/28 financial year. 
   Noting that the following projects be considered separately: 
  1. PBB-00002693 Community Renewables Council Owned Sporting Clubs, new project to be included with an expenditure of $2.5m (refer item 4.1).
  2. PBB 00002653 - Bus Shelter Installation - Stop 27 - Port Road - Cheltenham
  3. PBB 00002673 - Carnegie Reserve Sporting Precinct - Design and Consultation for New Public Toilet and Dog Park.


Carried 

Division called by Councillor - Kelly Thomas

Voters
For:Councillor - Edgar Agius, Councillor - Alice Campbell, Councillor - Senthil Chidambaranathan, Councillor - Stuart Ghent, Councillor - Katriona Kinsella, Councillor - Nicholas Le Lacheur, Councillor - Peter Ppiros, Councillor - Tom Scheffler, Councillor - Quin Tran, Councillor - Rachele Tullio, Councillor - George Turelli (11)
Against:Councillor - Merlindie Fardone, Councillor - Kelly Thomas, Councillor - Kenzie van den Nieuwelaar (3)
Not Vote:Mayor Angela Evans (1)
The Motion was Carried




Moved: Councillor Alice CampbellSeconded: Councillor Nicholas Le Lacheur

Motion

  1. That the following project be included in the Capital New and Upgrade program:

  • PBB-00002693 Community Renewables Council Owned Sporting Clubs, new project to be included with an expenditure of $2.5m (refer item 4.1).

  1. That Council include an explanation in the adopted Annual Business Plan outlining this amendment.
Carried 

Division called by Mayor Angela Evans

Voters
For:Councillor - Edgar Agius, Councillor - Alice Campbell, Councillor - Senthil Chidambaranathan, Councillor - Stuart Ghent, Councillor - Katriona Kinsella, Councillor - Nicholas Le Lacheur, Councillor - Peter Ppiros, Councillor - Tom Scheffler, Councillor - Quin Tran, Councillor - Rachele Tullio (10)
Against:Councillor - Merlindie Fardone, Councillor - Kelly Thomas, Councillor - George Turelli, Councillor - Kenzie van den Nieuwelaar (4)
Not Vote:Mayor Angela Evans (1)
The Motion was Carried


Moved: Councillor Kelly ThomasSeconded: Councillor Nicholas Le Lacheur

Motion

  1. That the following project name and scope from the Capital New and Upgrade program be included and updated as follows:

  • PPBB 00002673 - Carnegie Reserve Sporting Precinct - Design and Consultation for New Public Toilet and Dog Park be renamed to Carnegie Reserve Sporting Precinct - Design and Consultation for New Public Toilet and Amenities for Site Users.
Carried Unanimously



Moved: Councillor Senthil ChidambaranathanSeconded: Councillor Alice Campbell

Motion

  1. That the following project be included in the Capital New and Upgrade program:

  • PBB 00002653 - Bus Shelter Installation - Stop 27 - Port Road - Cheltenham
Lost

Councillor - Rachele Tullio left the meeting at 8:54 PM.



Moved: Councillor Alice CampbellSeconded: Councillor Nicholas Le Lacheur

Motion

  1. That Annual Operating Projects totalling $4,909,000 expenditure and $75,000 income as set out in Appendix 3 to the report, be provided for in the 2026/27 Budget, noting the following changes to budget following community consultation:
    1. PBB-00002611 Karrawirra Pari / Grange Creek – Cultural Interpretation, budget reduced from $65,000 to $0 as per CL 11/5/2026, item 6.1, due to a grant received (project remains included in reporting for transparency). 
    2. PBB-00002608 Graduate Program, expenditure budget reduced by $50,000 ($420,000 down to $370,000).
 
Carried 


Moved: Councillor Alice CampbellSeconded: Councillor Nicholas Le Lacheur

Motion
 
  1. That a recurrent operating expenditure budget of $170,424,288 (including depreciation) as summarised within the report be provided for in the 2026/27 Budget.
 
  1. That recurrent operating income budget of $19,656,351 (excluding rates levied) as summarised within the report be provided for in the 2026/27 budget.
 
  1. That net rates revenue of $156,789,101 (based on the endorsed LTFP Scenario (refer CL 10/3/2026, item 2.2.2/4.1) which assumed an average rates increase of 5.11% plus 1.1% forecast growth) as summarised within the report below (item 4.4) be provided for in the 2026/27 budget.
Carried 


Moved: Councillor Alice Campbell

Councillor - Rachele Tullio entered the meeting at 9:03 PM.

Seconded: Councillor Nicholas Le Lacheur

4.4. - PROPOSED RATING STRATEGY 2026/27

Motion 
 
That the Committee recommend to Council:
 
   1.  That the report be received and noted.
 
   2.  That the adopted rates model for 2026/27 assumes a relative distribution across all land use codes based on:
   
  • Option 3 - with legislative maximum of 35% of rate payers on the minimum rate, residential land use with an average rate increase of 4.58%, and all other land uses with the same approximate average rate increase of 5.11%, with the minimum rate is set to 4.52% and with an Operating Surplus of $2.54M (Operating Surplus ratio of 1.4%).
 
   3. That the rate relief options as listed below (and detailed further in the report) be incorporated into the Rating Policy:
  • Rate Capping
  • Residential Construction
  • Postponement of Rates
  • Hardship
 
  1. That a further report be presented to Council reflecting the preferred final rating scenario(s) utilising the final property valuations provided by the Valuer General in the form required by the Act, and which will also support the final recurrent budget to be reviewed and endorsed by Council.
Carried 
Division called by Councillor - Kelly Thomas

Voters
For:Councillor - Edgar Agius, Councillor - Alice Campbell, Councillor - Senthil Chidambaranathan, Councillor - Stuart Ghent, Councillor - Katriona Kinsella, Councillor - Nicholas Le Lacheur, Councillor - Peter Ppiros, Councillor - Tom Scheffler, Councillor - Quin Tran, Councillor - Rachele Tullio, Councillor - George Turelli (11)
Against:Councillor - Merlindie Fardone, Councillor - Kelly Thomas, Councillor - Kenzie van den Nieuwelaar (3)
Not Vote:Mayor Angela Evans (1)
The Motion was Carried



Moved: Councillor Alice Campbell
Seconded: Councillor Peter Ppiros

Motion

That Council does not adjourn for a break in accordance with the Code of Practice for Meeting Procedures and continue until the conclusion of the agenda.
Carried Unanimously

Leave of the meeting was sought to bring forward Item 6.1. Leave was granted.

A petition has been received from\u202FMr Benjamin Crago requesting that Council\u202Frefuse the development application 26000859 (at 15 Monmouth Street, Ridleyton), or at a minimum require substantial redesign to address concerns (as listed in Appendix 1). In relation to this development application the City of Charles Sturt's Assessment Manager is the relevant authority and as such Council has no authority to make a decision or request in relation to this matter. 

Councillor - Nicholas Le Lacheur left the meeting at 9:40 PM.
Councillor - Tom Scheffler entered the meeting at 9:40 PM.

General Declaration of Interest

Councillor - Peter Ppiros declared a general conflict of interest pursuant to Section 75B of the Local Government Act for Item 5.1. The nature of Councillor - Peter Ppiros' general conflict is that he is a member of the Council Assessment Panel. Councillor - Peter Ppiros dealt with the conflict of interest in the following transparent and accountable way and remaining in the room, sitting in the gallery for the duration of Item 5.1 and not participating in the debate or vote.

Moved: Councillor Katriona Kinsella
Seconded: Councillor George Turelli

Motion

  1. That Council receives the petition and acknowledges the concerns raised, however, notes it is not the relevant authority for a decision on this development matter and that the relevant authority is the City of Charles Sturt Assessment Manager.

  2. That the Council notes the petition has already been referred to the Assessment Manager for consideration.

  3. That Council notes the broader policy matter related to student accommodation developments within residential areas of the City of Charles Sturt and requests a report be presented to the Strategic and Engagement Committee in July 2026 outlining:
     
  1. the current planning and policy framework applicable to student accommodation developments, including the history and rationale for the introduction of the current policy settings;

  2. student accommodation development applications received within the City of Charles Sturt over the past five years, including application numbers, locations and outcomes;

  3. complaints, compliance matters and community feedback received by Council relating to student accommodation developments over the past five years; and

  4. if the City Plan (under development) will respond to such policy matters in future.
Carried Unanimously

A Motion on Notice has been received from Councillor Rachele Tullio seeking Council advocacy for increased service frequency on the Grange railway line and investigation of supporting infrastructure improvements to meet the needs of existing and future communities within the City of Charles Sturt.


Moved: Councillor Rachele Tullio
Seconded: Councillor Tom Scheffler

Motion

That Council:
 
  1. Acknowledges the importance of the Grange railway line as a key public transport corridor serving existing and future communities within the City of Charles Sturt.

  2. Recognises that service frequency is a key determinant of public transport usage and that increased service frequency on the Grange railway line would improve transport choice, connectivity and accessibility for residents.

  3. Requests that the Mayor write to the Hon. Joe Szakacs MP, Minister for Infrastructure and Transport, Aria Bolkus MP, Member for Colton, and David Wilkins MP, Member for Lee, seeking:
    1. an increase in Grange railway line services from hourly to half-hourly services on weekends and public holidays; and
    2. investigation of infrastructure improvements, including grade separation of the Port Road level crossing, to support increased rail service frequency and maintain the efficient movement of people, freight and public transport.
  1. Considers the future role of the Grange railway corridor, including service frequency improvements and associated infrastructure requirements, through the development of the City Plan and utilises the City Plan to inform future advocacy to the State Government.

Councillor - Katriona Kinsella entered the meeting at 9:54 PM.
Carried Unanimously

A Motion on Notice has been received from Councillor Senthil Chidambaranathan in relation to an increase in anti-social behaviour at Hills Smith Reserve in St Clair.


Moved: Councillor Senthil Chidambaranathan
Seconded: Councillor Peter Ppiros

Motion

That Council:

  1. Notes the Administration’s report and responses to the Questions on Notice tabled on 25 May 2026, which outlined the coordinated efforts of Council staff, SAPOL, DHS and partner agencies in addressing anti‑social behaviour at Cheltenham Racecourse Reserve.

  2. Acknowledges and thanks Council staff, SAPOL and supporting agencies for their ongoing work in responding to these complex issues and for their efforts to maintain safety, amenity and community confidence.

  3. Notes with concern that a new and significant incident of anti‑social behaviour has now occurred at Hills Smith Reserve in St Clair, resulting in disruptive noise, public drinking, aggressive behaviour, and families being unable to safely access the playground and open space.

  4. Recognises that this incident reflects a broader pattern of recurring behaviour across the St Clair precinct, impacting residents’ amenity, wellbeing and sense of safety.

  5. Requests Council staff provide practical and immediate solutions to manage and reduce anti‑social behaviour at Hills Smith Reserve and the surrounding area, and report these solutions back to Council.

  6. Requests Council staff engage directly with affected residents to ensure they are informed, supported and provided with clear pathways for reporting concerns.
Carried Unanimously

In accordance with the Local Government (Procedures at Meeting) Regulations I’m required to provide the Council with my decision to decline a deputation. I received a deputation request from Mr John Moskos for the meeting tonight regarding the Ocea Apartments at West Lakes on the following issues:

  • Car stacker systems: safety, certification, and the permanent disabling of 28 parking spaces. I determined to defer Mr Moskos’ request for the same reasons provided from 5 February 2026, that Council is awaiting a report from the Strata Corporation identifying the safety hazards. To date, this has not been provided to Council.
  • Mr Moskos also wished to speak with Council on building defects: roof drainage, potential fire compartmentation concerns, and insurability. I declined Mr Moskos’ request to speak to this point as Adelaide Strata and Community Management (ASCM) is the overarching strata group and Whittles manage the two commercial tenancies. Relevant staff have confirmed that Safework SA (acting in an advisory capacity) and ASCM were provided photographs and Service Certificates of the rectification works on 4 March 2026. This is not a matter for Council and future maintenance issues must be addressed appropriately through the strata corporation.
  • Mr Moskos also wished to speak with Council on parking: temporary mitigation for residents displaced by the loss of 28 spaces. I determined to defer Mr Moskos’ request for the same reasons provided from 5 February 2026, that Council is awaiting a report from the Strata Corporation identifying the safety hazards. To date, this has not been provided to Council.
  • Mr Moskos also wished to speak with Council on FOI 26/2025/2026: confirmed documentation void, construction-stage records, and procedural nullity. I declined Mr Moskos’ request to speak to this point as the application of the Freedom of Information Act falls outside of the authority of the Elected Body. In consultation with relevant staff it has been confirmed that Mr Moskos has invoked his right to an Internal Review under the same Act, and currently an External Review by the Ombudsman, pending their outcome.

Mr Moskos has stated that he intends to come to the meeting tonight and as the Members are aware you have the ability to move motion to overrule my decision and allow Mr Moskos to speak if he is in the gallery tonight.

At the Parks and Leisure Australia (SA/NT) Awards of Excellence on 3 June 2026, the City of Charles Sturt and Green Adelaide received two awards for the Breakout Creek Stage 3 / Purruna Pari project: the 'Environment and Sustainability Initiative' Award and 'Park of the Year' Award.

These awards recognise the project's success in restoring and enhancing the River Torrens corridor through environmental rehabilitation, biodiversity improvements, sustainable design and the creation of high-quality public open space. The achievement reflects the strong collaboration between Council staff, Green Adelaide, the City of West Torrens, contractors and the community in delivering a project that provides lasting environmental, recreational and community benefits.

General Declaration of Interest

Mayor Angela Evans declared a general conflict of interest pursuant to Section 75B of the Local Government Act for Item 6.1. The nature of Mayor Angela Evans' general conflict is that she is a Green Adelaide board member and the interest is indirect. Mayor Angela Evans dealt with the conflict of interest in the following transparent and accountable way and remained in the meeting, participating in the debate but not voting as a casting vote was not required.

Moved: Councillor Nicole Mazeika
Seconded: Councillor Merlindie Fardone

Motion

That Council:

  1. Notes that the City of Charles Sturt, in partnership with Green Adelaide and the City of West Torrens, has received two Parks and Leisure Australia (SA/NT) Awards of Excellence for the Breakout Creek Stage 3 / Purruna Pari Project, being:

    • Environment and Sustainability Initiative Award; and
    • Park of the Year Award.

  2. Congratulates and acknowledges the contribution of Council staff whose commitment, expertise and collaboration were instrumental in the successful delivery of this award-winning project.

Carried Unanimously

","reportContent":null,"minutesDiscussion":"Brief
This report seeks Council adoption of the Annual Business Plan and Budget 2026/27, following a comprehensive budget development and community consultation process. The proposed budget delivers Council’s strategic priorities through a balanced recurrent budget, a significant annual operating and capital works program, and a rating strategy that includes targeted rate relief measures to support the community.



Moved: Councillor Michael McEwen
Seconded: Councillor Nicole Mazeika

Motion

That in exercise of the powers contained in Chapters 9 and 10 of the Local Government Act 1999 (“the Act”) and in respect of the financial year ending 30 June 2027:
 
1. Annual Business Plan
 
In accordance with Section 123 of the Act and Regulation 6 of the Local Government (Financial Management) Regulations 2011 and having considered all submissions received, in accordance with Section 123(6) of the Act, the 2026/27 Annual Business Plan as set in the Annual Business Plan and Budget document, as detailed in Appendix 1 to the report, be adopted.
 
2. Adoption of Budget
 
In accordance with Section 123 of the Act and Regulation 7 of the Local Government (Financial Management) Regulations 2011, having considered the Budget in conjunction with, and determined the Budget to be consistent with, the Council’s Annual Business Plan, the Budget as detailed in Appendix 2, Schedules 1 to 6 and as laid before the Council at this meeting compliant with the Model Financial Statements, comprising:
 
  1. the budgeted Statement of Comprehensive Income;
  2. the budgeted Statement of Cash Flows;
  3. the budgeted Statement of Financial Position; 
  4. the budgeted Statement of Changes in Equity;
  5. the budgeted Summary of Operating and Capital Investment Activities (Uniform Presentation of Finances); and
  6. the budgeted statement of financial indicators be adopted, involving;
 
  1. A total estimated recurrent operating expenditure (including depreciation) of $170,424,288
  2. A total estimated recurrent operating income from sources other than rates levied of $19,656,351
  3. A total amount required to be levied from rates of $156,492,271 (excluding Regional Landscape Levy, and before rebates, fines & interest charges)
  4. A total estimated Capital Project works program of $56,721,988 (net)
  5. A total estimated Annual Operating project program of $4,834,000 (net)
 
be adopted.
 
3. Adoption of Valuations
 
That pursuant to Section 167(2)(a) of the Act, the most recent valuations of the Valuer-General available to the Council of the Capital Value of all land within the Council’s area, totalling $68,932,273,480 be adopted, of which $66,544,912,064 is for rating purposes.
 
4. General Rate – Maximum Increase
 
That pursuant to Section 153(3) of the Act the Council has determined not to fix a maximum increase in the general rate to be charged on any rateable land within its area that constitutes the principal place of residence of a principal ratepayer.
 
5. Declaration of General Rates
 
That, having taken into account the general principles of rating contained in Section 150 of the Act and the requirements of Section 153(2) of the Act, and in order to raise the amount in 2.6(c) above, the Council hereby determines that:
 
(1) differential general rates be declared in accordance with Sections 153(1)(b) and 156(1)(a) of the Act on the capital value of all rateable land within the Council area and varying according to the use of the land as follows:
 
Rateable Land CategoryCents in the Dollar
Residential0.170947733
Commercial – shop, office & other use0.6447867390
Industry – light & other0.6533230370
Primary Production0.5503389830
Vacant Land0.530469271
Other0.3287773770
 
(2) pursuant to section 158(1)(a) of the Act, a minimum amount payable by way of general rates of $1,410 be fixed for rateable land within the Council area.
 
6. Declaration of Separate Rates – Regional Landscape Levy
 
In accordance with Section 69 of the Landscape South Australia Act 2019 and Section 154 of the Act, and in order to reimburse to Council, the amount contributed to the Green Adelaide Board being $3,832,049 a separate rate of 0.00588000 cents in the dollar, based on the Capital Value of rateable land, is declared on all rateable land in the Council’s area.
 
7. Payment
 
(1)  That pursuant to Section 181(2) of the Act, all rates payable in respect of the financial year ending on 30 June 2027 be payable in four equal or approximately equal instalments (unless otherwise agreed with the Principal Ratepayer) due on 1 September 2026, 1 December 2026, 1 March 2027 and 1 June 2027.
 
8. Rebates – Development
 
In exercise of the powers contained in Section 166 (1) (a) of the Act, and being of the opinion that it is desirable to do so for the purpose of securing the proper development of the area, a rebate of general rates is hereby granted in respect of an Assessment classed as vacant land in the Council’s Assessment Record at the date this resolution is passed, where:
 
(1) Residential Construction
The land is in a Residential Zone or a Residential Historic (Conservation) zone in the Development Plan applicable to the Council's area, the rebate being granted only if the following conditions are satisfied:
 
(a) the Principal Ratepayer in respect of the Assessment applies to the Council for the rebate prior to 30 June 2027; and
 
(b) construction of a dwelling has been substantially commenced on the Assessment by 30 June 2027; and
 
(c) the Council is satisfied that the intention of the Principal Ratepayer is to reside in that dwelling upon completion for at least 1 year;
 
with the amount of the rebate being the difference in monetary terms between the rates that would have been paid in respect of the Assessment if it had been used at the date of declaration of the rates for residential purposes and the actual amount paid after deducting any other rebate granted within the rating period, subject to the following:
 
(a) if footings are poured prior to 31 December 2026 a rebate of the entire amount will be given; and
 
(b) if footings are poured after 31 December 2026 a rebate of 50% of that amount will be given.
 
9.   Rebate - Rate Capping
 
That in exercise of the powers contained in Section 166(1)(I) of the Act and to provide relief against what would otherwise amount to a substantial change in rates payable by a ratepayer due to rapid changes in valuation, a rebate of general rates will be granted to the Principal Ratepayer of an Assessment where the amount of any increase in rates in respect of that Assessment between the amount of general rates imposed for the financial year ending on 30 June 2027 and the amount of general rates payable for the financial year ending 30 June 2026 (after any rebate was applied) is greater than 12.5 percent;
 
Provided, however, that the rebate shall not apply where:
 
(a) any such increase in rates is due or partly due to an increase in valuation of the land in the Assessment because of improvements made to it worth more than $20,000; or
 
(b) any such increase in rates is applicable to the use of the land being the categories of commercial, industrial, primary production, vacant land and other; or
 
(c) the ownership of the rateable property has changed since 1 July 2025.
 
The amount of the rebate being the difference between the amount of general rates in monetary terms imposed for the financial year ending on 30 June 2027 and the amount of rates in monetary terms payable (after any rebate was applied but prior to deducting concessions) for the financial year ending on 30 June 2026 plus 12.5 percent of those rates.

 

10. Rating Policy
 
That the revised Rating Policy, as detailed in Appendix 3 to the report, be adopted.
 
Carried 
Division called by Councillor Kelly Thomas

Voters
For:Councillor - Edgar Agius, Councillor - Alice Campbell, Councillor -Senthil Chidambaranathan, Councillor -Stuart Ghent, Councillor -Katriona Kinsella, Councillor -Nicole Mazeika, Councillor -Michael McEwen, Councillor -Peter Ppiros, Councillor - Tom Scheffler, Councillor -Quin Tran, Councillor - Rachele Tullio, Councillor - George Turelli (12)
Against:Councillor - Merlindie Fardone, Councillor - Kelly Thomas (2)
Not Vote:Mayor Angela Evans (1)
The Motion to Item 6.2. was Carried

The City of Charles Sturt acknowledges and pays respect to the traditional custodians of the land, the Kaurna people of the Adelaide plains. We pay our respect to Elders past, present and emerging. We respect their spiritual beliefs and connections to land which are of continuing importance to the Kaurna people of today. We acknowledge the contributions and important role that Aboriginal people continue to play within our local community in Charles Sturt. We also respect the culture of Aboriginal people visiting from other areas of South Australia and Australia.

Almighty Father from Whom all goodness flows, grant unto us qualities of wisdom justice and tolerance, that we the civic leaders of this community may govern in harmony and concord.

This we ask in Thy name. 

We also remember and give thanks for those, our sons and daughters, who gave their lives for Australia.

The Strategic and Engagement Committee was held on Monday, 15 June 2026.


Moved: Councillor Nicole Mazeika
Seconded: Councillor Peter Ppiros

That having considered the recommendations of the Committee which has read and considered the reports in the agenda related to all items, with the exception of Items 4.2, 4.5 and 4.6:

 

3.1 DEPUTATION - REQUEST TO PURCHASE A PORTION OF COUNCIL OWNED LAND WITHIN PARFITT SQUARE RESERVE, BROMPTON

Motion
 
  1. That the deputation be received and noted. 
 
  1. That Mr Matthew Sauer be thanked for his presentation and any notes that comply with Council's Code of Practice for Meeting Procedures and the laws of defamation, be included in the Minutes.
 
4.1. - PRESENTATION - FUTURE CITY PLAN - UPDATE
 
Motion
 
 That the Committee recommends that:
 
  1. The Future City Plan presentation be received and noted, and a copy included in the minutes of the meeting.
 
  1. That the report be received and noted.
 

4.3. - TORRENS TO DARLINGTON (T2D) - PROJECT UPDATE AND PRESENTATION
 
Motion
 
 1. That the Strategic and Engagement Committee recommends that Council:
 
  1. Receives and notes the presentation.
 
  1. Accepts the future transfer of the Karrawirra Parri footbridge and associated assets from the Department for Infrastructure and Transport (DIT), subject to completion of the defect liability and maintenance period and execution of the associated deed documentation.
 
  1. Authorise the Mayor and Chief Executive Officer to sign, seal and deal with all documentation required to give effect to this resolution, including the execution and sealing of the Deeds attached at Appendix 1 and Appendix 2.
 
  1. Requests the Mayor write to the Minister for Infrastructure and Transport seeking a meeting and further information regarding future City Shaping Fund opportunities and partnership funding pathways for projects identified through the West Hindmarsh, Welland and Hindmarsh Your Neighbourhood Plan.
 
  1. That the Strategic and Engagement Committee recommends that Council notes that:
 
  1. Future revisions to relevant Asset Management Plans and the Long-Term Financial Plan will incorporate the contributed assets associated with the Torrens to Darlington Project following asset handover;
 
  1. The compulsory acquisition process associated with Langman Reserve remains ongoing and discussions continue with the Department for Infrastructure and Transport regarding compensation and future outcomes for the site;
 
  1. A portion of air stratum above the Hindmarsh Cemetery has been compulsorily acquired; and
 
  1. Advocacy has been undertaken in response to previous Council resolutions, including engagement with the State Government regarding shared funding opportunities for projects identified through the West Hindmarsh, Welland and Hindmarsh Your Neighbourhood Plan. 
 
4.4. - COUNCIL RESPONSE TO CREATIVE AUSTRALIA NATIONAL CULTURAL POLICY CONSULTATION
 
Motion
 
 That the Committee recommends that Council:
 
  1. Notes the submission made by the City of Charles Sturt to the National Cultural Policy consultation.
 
4.7. - CONSULTATION OUTCOMES - REQUEST TO PURCHASE COUNCIL LAND - PARFITT SQUARE RESERVE, BROMPTON
 
Motion 
 
Acknowledging the exceptional nature of this matter and that the proposal seeks to regularise a longstanding anomaly rather than establish a precedent, the Strategy and Engagement Committee recommends to Council:
 
  1. That the Community Engagement Summary Report (Appendix 1) relating to the proposed revocation of community land classification and sale of a portion of Parfitt Square Reserve, Bowden, be received and noted.
 
  1. That Council, having considered the submissions received and the requirements of section 194 of the Local Government Act 1999, resolves to seek the consent of the Minister for Local Government to revoke the community land classification over approximately 83.34 square metres of Lot 1003 in Filed Plan 31310 (Certificate of Title Volume 5151 Folio 893), as identified in Appendix 2.
 
  1. That, subject to obtaining the consent of the Minister for Local Government, Council revoke the community land classification of the land identified in Appendix 2 and retain ownership of the land until a development approval for 109 Drayton Street, Bowden has been granted. The approved development must be substantially the same as, or reasonably consistent with, the proposal submitted to Council by the registered proprietor and contained in Appendix.
 
  1. That, upon satisfaction of Recommendation 3, Council sell the land described in Recommendation 2 to the current registered proprietor of 109 Drayton Street, Bowden for $125,000 (excluding GST), provided settlement occurs within twelve (12) months of the date of this resolution. Should Recommendation 3 not be satisfied within that period, an updated market valuation is to be obtained and the purchaser shall be required to purchase the land at the revised valuation.
 
  1. That the current registered proprietor of 109 Drayton Street, Bowden be responsible for all costs associated with the revocation of the community land classification, sale of the land, and boundary realignment process, including but not limited to public consultation costs, legal expenses, survey and land division costs, and registration fees.
 
  1. That the Mayor and Chief Executive Officer be authorised to execute all documents and take all actions necessary to give effect to this resolution. 
                                             
 
4.8. - RESPONSE TO PETITION - IMPROVEMENTS AT LINES RESERVE, GRANGE
 
Motion 
 
 That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That Council notes that minor improvements at Lines Reserve in 2026/27 will be delivered through existing recurrent budgets and operational programs, including provision of habitat logs, maintenance of the basketball court surface and continuation of routine weed and turf management.
 
  1. That Council undertake targeted community engagement and develop a concept design in 2026/27 to investigate potential improvements at Lines Reserve, including a BBQ and shelter, additional bin provision, soccer training goals, planting and a perimeter pathway, with any future works subject to Council consideration as part of the 2027/28 budget process.
 
  1. That the head petitioner be advised of Council’s decision.
 
4.9. - COUNCIL ASSESSMENT PANEL MARCH 2026 END OF QUARTER REPORT
 
Motion
 
 That the Committee recommends to Council that:
 
  1. The report be received and noted.

 

Council adopts the recommendations of the Committee as printed in the Minutes of this Committee.

Carried Unanimously


Moved: Councillor Nicole Mazeika
Seconded: Councillor Senthil Chidambaranathan

4.2. - PRESENTATION - CARBON REPORTING AND EMISSIONS REDUCTION PLAN 
 
Motion
 
 That the Strategic and Engagement Committee recommends to Council:
 
  1. That Council endorses the City of Charles Sturt Emissions Reduction Plan 2026-2031 as contained in Attachment 1.
 
  1. That Council notes the Plan establishes emissions reduction targets aligned with a Science Based Targets approach, Council's Climate Change Response Plan 2024-2030 and provides a framework for reducing operational emissions across Council activities.
 
  1. That through existing reporting mechanisms, Administration provide annual progress reports to Council on implementation of the Plan and progress towards emissions reduction targets.
 
  1. That the presentation be received and noted, a copy included in the minutes of the meeting, and presented to Council at its Ordinary Meeting on the 22nd of June. 
Carried Unanimously


Moved: Councillor Katriona Kinsella
Seconded: Councillor Alice Campbell

4.5. - PLACE NAMING PROJECT
 
Motion 

That the Council defer a decision on the consolidated list of place names, as provided in Appendix 2, for use across the Bowden, Brompton and Hindmarsh area for the purposes of establishing a pre-approved “name bank” to support future naming of road, reserves and public places.

Further, the Council requests a report be brought back to the Strategic & Engagement Committee that:
 
1. Articulates and/or incorporates the proposed approach to Kaurna naming as applicable;
 
2. Updates the Place Naming Methodology to consider presentation of the draft list of proposed names to targeted and/or agreed stakeholders for feedback; and
 
3. Outlines an updated list of recommended names from the feedback received from stakeholder engagement for the Bowden, Brompton and Hindmarsh area.
Carried Unanimously


Moved: Councillor Merlindie Fardone
Seconded: Councillor Nicole Mazeika

4.6. - EVENT GRANTS & EVENT SPONSORSHIP: REQUESTS FOR FUNDING
 
Motion
 
That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That Council approves the following events for funding as Event Grants:
    • Adelaide Ceramic Fair - Adelaide Ceramic Fair
    • Philippine Fiesta of South Australia - Philippine Fiesta
    • Shruthi Adelaide - Nritya Vaibhavam (Grandeur of Dance)
    • Sree Narayana Mission Adelaide – Onam
    • Tennyson Dunes Group - Wara Wayingga Tennyson Dunes Open Day
 
Carried Unanimously

The Operations Committee was held on Monday, 15 June 2026.


Moved: Councillor Senthil Chidambaranathan
Seconded: Councillor Stuart Ghent

That having considered the recommendations of the Committee which has read and considered the reports in the agenda related to items:

 

4.1. - KNIGHT STREET, ALLENBY GARDENS - PARKING REVIEW AND PROPOSED CHANGES TO PARKING CONTROLS
Motion 
 
 That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That Council endorse the recommended amendments (Option 3) to the existing parking controls in Knight Street, Allenby Gardens to:
    1. relocate the current school peak parking restrictions from the northern side of the street to the southern side of the street between East Avenue and Lewanick Street.
    2. amended restriction on the southern side be changed from “No Parking” to “No Stopping” during school peak periods to improve driveway access, manoeuvrability and traffic safety.
 
  1. That Council note staff have undertaken direct consultation with affected residents and have been unable to achieve consensus on a preferred outcome.
 
  1. That Council note the proposed arrangement seeks to balance competing resident access needs, school traffic demand, road safety considerations and equitable use of available on-street parking and is consistent with the objectives of Council's Parking Controls Policy.
 
  1. That administration proceed with implementation of the amended parking controls should Council endorse the recommendation.
 
4.2. - MIRANI COURT VIEWING PLATFORM, SEMAPHORE PARK
 
Motion 
 
 That the Committee recommends to the Council:
 
  1. That based on the most recent advice received from the Coast Protection Board, the Mirani Court Viewing Platform project at Semaphore Park does not proceed.
 
  1. That the funds allocated to the project in the 2025/26 financial year be identified as savings as part of a future budget review process.
 
  1. That Council notes that, as part of future coastal asset renewal and construction projects, Administration will investigate opportunities to incorporate accessible viewing platforms into project scopes where feasible, appropriate and capable of achieving the necessary regulatory approvals.
 
4.3. - CITY OPERATIONS CAPITAL WORKS & OPERATING PROGRAM VARIATIONS
 
Motion 
 
 That the Committee recommends to the Council: 
 
  1. That the following variations to the Capital Works Program or Annual Operating Program be approved and adjusted in the budget and annual financial statements 2025/26 as they involve transfers between renewal and new/upgrade works and or new projects to be funded by unbudgeted income: 
     
     a. Budgeted expenditure for Woodville South Football Club - Changerooms (Project 3614 – Upgrade) be increased by $100,000 from savings in the 2025/26 Council Building Renewals - (Project 3824 – Renewal). 
      
     b. Budgeted expenditure for Mick Harley Reserve (Project 3646 - Upgrade) be increased by $50,000 from savings in the 2025/26 Council Building Renewals (Project 3824 - Renewal).
      
  2. That the following variations to the Capital Works Program be approved and budgets or scope adjusted accordingly:
     
     a. Project scope for the AMP Fences, Walls and Bollard Renewals – 2025/26 (Project 3629 - Renewal) be updated to include construction of a new fence as part of the Gordon Street Reserve Upgrade in Albert Park, with no change to budget.

  3. That by endorsing the variations listed in 1. above, Council is endorsing a variation to the approved Asset Management Plan renewal schedule where relevant.

 

Council adopts the recommendations of the Committee as printed in the Minutes of this Committee.

Carried Unanimously

To seek Council's endorsement to pursue an Expression of Interest to the South Australian Government's Multicultural Community Fund for the construction of an outdoor community kitchen at Cheltenham Community Centre.



Moved: Councillor Quin Tran
Seconded: Councillor Senthil Chidambaranathan

Motion

  1. That Council endorses submission of an Expression of Interest to the South Australian Government’s Multicultural Community Fund (MCF) for the construction of an outdoor community kitchen facility at Cheltenham Community Centre.

The City of Charles Sturt acknowledges and pays respect to the traditional custodians of the land, the Kaurna people of the Adelaide plains. We pay our respect to Elders past, present and emerging. We respect their spiritual beliefs and connections to land which are of continuing importance to the Kaurna people of today. We acknowledge the contributions and important role that Aboriginal people continue to play within our local community in Charles Sturt. We also respect the culture of Aboriginal people visiting from other areas of South Australia and Australia.

Almighty Father from Whom all goodness flows, grant unto us qualities of wisdom justice and tolerance, that we the civic leaders of this community may govern in harmony and concord.

This we ask in Thy name. 

We also remember and give thanks for those, our sons and daughters, who gave their lives for Australia. 

Lest we forget.

Regulation 21 of the Local Government (Procedures at Meetings) Regulations 2013 enables the Chief Executive Officer to submit a report to Council recommending the revocation or amendment of a resolution passed since the last general election of the Council. Following the delay of the next Periodic Local Government Elections until April 2027, this report seeks to amend Council's previous decision relating to the appointment of Councillor Kinsella as Deputy Mayor (refer CL 24/11/25, Item 6.3). The previous resolution of Council appointed Councillor Kinsella as Deputy Mayor until the conclusion of the 2026 Periodic Local Government Elections. As the conclusion date is no longer 2026 this report seeks to amend Council's previous decision to make the appointment conclusion date 'until the conclusion of the next Periodic Local Government Elections'. 

Material Declaration of Interest
Councillor - Katriona Kinsella declared a material conflict of interest pursuant to Section 75C of the Local Government Act for Item 6.3. The nature of Councillor Kinsella's material conflict is that she is the currently in the position of Deputy Mayor and left the meeting.

Councillor - Katriona Kinsella left the meeting at 7:36 PM.

Moved: Councillor Alice Campbell
Seconded: Councillor Peter Ppiros

Motion

  1. That the Council resolves to conclude the current term of Deputy Mayor on 13 November 2026.

  2. That an appointment for the term of Deputy Mayor from 14 November 2026, until the end of the Council term, be made in the Council meeting on Monday 12 October 2026.
Carried
